عَنْ رَجُلٍ يَخْرُجُ مِنْ ذَكَرِهِ قَيْحٌ لَا يَنْقَطِعُ:
 فَهَلْ تَصِحُّ صَلَاتُهُ مَعَ خُرُوجِ ذَلِكَ؟ أَفْتُونَا مَأْجُورِينَ.
فَأَجَابَ:
 لَا يَجُوزُ أَنْ يُبْطِلَ الصَّلَاةَ بَلْ يُصَلِّي بِحَسَبِ إمْكَانِهِ.
 فَإِنْ لَمْ تَنْقَطِعْ النَّجَاسَةُ قَدْرَ مَا يَتَوَضَّأُ وَيُصَلِّي:
 صَلَّى بِحَسَبِ حَالِهِ بَعْدَ أَنْ يَتَوَضَّأَ وَإِنْ خَرَجَتْ النَّجَاسَةُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ لَكِنْ يَتَّخِذُ حِفَاظًا يَمْنَعُ مِنْ انْتِشَارِ النَّجَاسَةِ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَمَّا إذَا تَوَضَّأَ وَقَامَ يُصَلِّي وَأَحَسَّ بِالنُّقْطَةِ فِي صَلَاتِهِ:
 فَهَلْ تَبْطُلُ صَلَاتُهُ أَمْ لَا؟ .
translated_text:
Chapter: Things That Invalidate Ablution

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

A man has a continuous discharge of pus from his penis. Is his prayer valid while this discharge continues? Please give us a ruling, and may you be rewarded.

He replied:

He must not abandon prayer; rather, he should pray as best he can. If the discharge of impurity does not stop long enough for him to perform ablution and pray, he should perform ablution and then pray as his condition permits, even if the impurity is discharged during prayer. However, he should use a protective covering to prevent the impurity from spreading. Allah knows best.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

If someone performs ablution, stands to pray, and feels a drop during his prayer, is his prayer invalidated or not?

original_text:
فَأَجَابَ:
 مُجَرَّدُ الْإِحْسَاسِ لَا يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ؛ وَلَا يَجُوزُ لَهُ الْخُرُوجُ مِنْ الصَّلَاةِ الْوَاجِبَةِ بِمُجَرَّدِ الشَّكِّ؛ فَإِنَّهُ قَدْ ثَبَتَ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ 
{أَنَّهُ سُئِلَ عَنْ الرَّجُلِ يَجِدْ الشَّيْءَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ؟
 فَقَالَ:
 لَا يَنْصَرِفُ حَتَّى يَسْمَعَ صَوْتًا أَوْ يَجِدَ رِيحًا}
 . وَأَمَّا إذَا تَيَقَّنَ خُرُوجَ الْبَوْلِ إلَى ظَاهِرِ الذَّكَرِ فَقَدْ انْتَقَضَ وُضُوءُهُ وَعَلَيْهِ الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ إلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ بِهِ سَلَسُ الْبَوْلِ فَلَا تَبْطُلُ الصَّلَاةُ بِمُجَرَّدِ ذَلِكَ إذَا فَعَلَ مَا أُمِرَ بِهِ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ أَيْضًا - رَحِمَهُ اللَّهُ -:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ كُلَّمَا شَرَعَ فِي الصَّلَاةِ يَحْدُثُ لَهُ رِيَاحٌ كَثِيرَةٌ؛ حَتَّى فِي الصَّلَاةِ يَتَوَضَّأُ أَرْبَعَ مَرَّاتٍ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ؛ إلَى حِينِ يَقْضِي الصَّلَاةَ يَزُولُ عَنْهُ الْعَارِضُ؛ ثُمَّ لَا يَعُودُ إلَيْهِ إلَّا فِي أَوْقَاتِ الصَّلَاةِ وَهُوَ لَا يَعْلَمُ مَا سَبَبُ ذَلِكَ؟
 :
 هَلْ هُوَ مِنْ شِدَّةِ حِرْصِهِ عَلَى الطَّهَارَةِ؟ وَقَدْ يَشُقُّ عَلَيْهِ كَثْرَةُ الْوُضُوءِ وَمَا يَعْلَمُ هَلْ حُكْمُهُ حُكْمُ صَاحِبِ الْأَعْذَارِ أَمْ لَا لِسَبَبِ أَنَّهُ لَا يُعَاوِدُهُ إلَّا فِي وَقْتِ الصَّلَاةِ؟ وَمَا تَطِيبُ نَفْسُهُ أَنْ يُصَلِّيَ بِوُضُوءِ وَاحِدٍ؟ .
translated_text:
He replied:

A mere sensation does not invalidate ablution, nor may he leave an obligatory prayer merely because of doubt. It is established that the Prophet “was asked about a man who feels something during prayer, and he said: ‘He should not leave until he hears a sound or detects an odor.’”

However, if he is certain that urine has emerged from his penis, his ablution is invalidated, and he must cleanse himself, unless he suffers from urinary incontinence. In that case, this alone does not invalidate his prayer, provided he has done what he was instructed to do. Allah knows best.

He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

A man experiences frequent flatulence whenever he begins praying, to the point that he performs ablution four times or more in the course of the prayer. Once he finishes the prayer, the condition subsides and does not return until prayer time. He does not know what causes it. Is it due to his intense concern for ritual purity? Repeated ablution can be difficult for him, and he does not know whether the ruling for those with legally recognized excuses applies to him, since this condition recurs only at prayer time. Moreover, he does not feel at ease praying with just one ablution.

original_text:
فَأَجَابَ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ -:
نَعَمْ،
 حُكْمُهُ حُكْمُ أَهْلِ الْأَعْذَارِ:
 مِثْلِ الِاسْتِحَاضَةِ وَسَلَسِ الْبَوْلِ؛ وَالْمَذْيِ؛ وَالْجُرْحِ الَّذِي لَا يَرْقَأُ؛ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ. فَمَنْ لَمْ يُمْكِنْهُ حِفْظُ الطَّهَارَةِ مِقْدَارَ الصَّلَاةِ فَإِنَّهُ يَتَوَضَّأُ وَيُصَلِّي وَلَا يَضُرُّهُ مَا خَرَجَ مِنْهُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ وَلَا يَنْتَقِضُ وَضَوْءُهُ بِذَلِكَ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْأَئِمَّةِ وَأَكْثَرُ مَا عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يَتَوَضَّأَ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ. وَقَدْ تَنَازَعَ الْعُلَمَاءُ فِي الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ وَمَنْ بِهِ سَلَسُ الْبَوْلِ وَأَمْثَالُهُمَا مِثْلُ مَنْ بِهِ رِيحٌ يَخْرُجُ عَلَى غَيْرِ الْوَجْهِ الْمُعْتَادِ؛ وَكُلُّ مَنْ بِهِ حَدَثٌ نَادِرٌ.
 فَمَذْهَبُ مَالِكٍ:
 أَنَّ ذَلِكَ يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ بِالْحَدَثِ الْمُعْتَادِ. وَلَكِنَّ الْجُمْهُورَ - كَأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ؛ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ؛ وَأَحْمَد بْنِ حَنْبَلٍ -
 يَقُولُونَ:
 إنَّهُ يَتَوَضَّأُ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ أَوْ لِوَقْتِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ. رَوَاهُ أَهْلُ السُّنَنِ وَصَحَّحَ ذَلِكَ غَيْرُ وَاحِدٍ مِنْ الْحُفَّاظِ؛ فَلِهَذَا كَانَ أَظْهَرَ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ أَنَّ مِثْلَ هَؤُلَاءِ يَتَوَضَّئُونَ لِكُلِّ صَلَاةٍ أَوْ لِوَقْتِ كُلِّ صَلَاةٍ.
وَأَمَّا مَا يَخْرُجُ فِي الصَّلَاةِ دَائِمًا فَهَذَا لَا يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْعُلَمَاءِ.
 وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ:
 أَنَّ بَعْضَ أَزْوَاجِ النَّبِيِّ كَانَتْ تُصَلِّي وَالدَّمُ يَقْطُرُ مِنْهَا؛ فَيُوضَعُ لَهَا طَسْتٌ يَقْطُرُ فِيهِ الدَّمُ. وَثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ أَنَّ عُمَرَ بْنَ الْخَطَّابِ - رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ - صَلَّى وَجُرْحُهُ يَثْعَبُ دَمًا. وَمَا زَالَ الْمُسْلِمُونَ عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ يُصَلُّونَ فِي جِرَاحَاتِهِمْ.
translated_text:
He replied—may Allah be pleased with him:

Yes. The ruling for those with legally recognized excuses applies to him, as in cases of non-menstrual bleeding, urinary incontinence, discharge of pre-ejaculatory fluid, a wound that will not stop bleeding, and similar conditions. Whoever cannot maintain ritual purity long enough to perform the prayer should perform ablution and pray. Whatever comes out of him during prayer does not affect his prayer or invalidate his ablution, by agreement of the imams. At most, he is required to perform ablution for each prayer.

The scholars have differed concerning a woman with non-menstrual bleeding, someone with urinary incontinence, and others in comparable circumstances, such as someone who passes wind in an abnormal manner, or anyone experiencing an uncommon occurrence of ritual impurity. According to Mālik, such a person’s ablution is invalidated by an ordinary occurrence of ritual impurity. The majority, however—including Abū Hanīfah, al-Shāfi‘ī, and Ahmad ibn Hanbal—hold that such a person should perform ablution for each prayer, or for the time of each prayer. This was transmitted by the compilers of the Sunan and authenticated by several leading hadith scholars. Thus, the stronger of the two scholarly positions is that people with such conditions should perform ablution for each prayer, or for the time of each prayer.

As for what continually comes out during prayer, this does not invalidate ablution, by agreement of the scholars. It is established in an authentic report that one of the Prophet’s wives would pray while blood dripped from her, and a basin would be placed beneath her to catch it. It is also established in an authentic report that ‘Umar ibn al-Khattāb—may Allah be pleased with him—prayed while blood flowed from his wound. Throughout the Prophet’s lifetime, Muslims would pray despite their wounds.

original_text:
وَقَدْ تَنَازَعَ الْعُلَمَاءُ فِي خُرُوجِ النَّجَاسَةِ مِنْ غَيْرِ السَّبِيلَيْنِ -
 كَالْجُرْحِ وَالْفِصَادِ وَالْحِجَامَةِ وَالرُّعَافِ وَالْقَيْءِ:
 فَمَذْهَبُ مَالِكٍ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ: لَا يَنْقُضُ.

The scholars have differed over whether impurity discharged from somewhere other than the front and rear passages—such as through a wound, venesection, cupping, a nosebleed, or vomiting—invalidates ablution. Mālik and al-Shāfi‘ī hold that it does not, while Abū Hanīfah and Ahmad hold that it does. Ahmad, however, stipulates that the quantity must be substantial.

They have also differed over whether touching women or touching the penis invalidates ablution. Abū Hanīfah holds that it does not, while al-Shāfi‘ī holds that it does. Mālik distinguishes between touching with desire and touching without it, though reports from him differ as to whether this distinction applies to touching the penis. Reports from Ahmad also differ: one agrees with Abū Hanīfah that none of these acts invalidates ablution, while two other reports agree with Mālik and al-Shāfi‘ī respectively.

The early Muslims differed over whether ablution is obligatory after eating food cooked over fire. They also differed concerning laughing aloud during prayer; Abū Hanīfah holds that it invalidates ablution. Those who maintain that these things do not invalidate ablution have two views on whether performing ablution after them is recommended. Both views are found in the school of Ahmad and elsewhere.

The stronger view in all these cases is that they do not invalidate ablution, but that performing ablution after them is recommended. Whoever prays without renewing ablution after them has a valid prayer, while whoever performs ablution does what is better. The evidence for this is discussed at length elsewhere. For Allah Most High says:

“Allah does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.”

And He says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

The Prophet said:

“When I command you to do something, do as much of it as you can.”

Any obligation of prayer that a person is unable to fulfil is waived for him. He may not delay the prayer beyond its appointed time; rather, he must pray within that time as best he can. However, most scholars permit him to combine two prayers for a valid excuse. Indeed, according to the stronger of the scholars’ two views, combining prayers is permissible for the sick, women experiencing non-menstrual bleeding, and others with valid excuses. Thus, the Prophet recommended that a woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding combine the noon and afternoon prayers with a single ritual bath. For a person with a valid excuse, even if he can combine the two prayers with a single purification without any discharge occurring during prayer, combining them is permissible according to the stronger of the scholars’ two views. Likewise, a sick person may combine prayers with a single purification if purifying himself for each prayer would worsen his illness.

Prayer must be performed within its appointed time, with purification using water if possible, and otherwise with dry ablution. Anyone who cannot find water, or fears harm from using it because of illness or severe cold, may perform dry ablution, even if he is in a state of major ritual impurity. Whoever sleeps through a prayer or forgets it, let him pray it when he remembers it.” These matters are discussed at length elsewhere.

The point here is to explain that Allah Most High has imposed no hardship on Muslims in their religion. Rather, He, glorified be He, intends ease for them and does not intend hardship for them. The case raised by this questioner is even more deserving of a dispensation; hence the scholars agree on it. These matters are discussed at length in other places. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

About a man who performs the five daily prayers without fail but does not attend Friday prayer. He explains that he does not attend because he experiences wind in his abdomen that prevents him from waiting for Friday prayer. His home is about two miles or less from the place where Friday prayer is held.

Is the excuse he has mentioned sufficient to justify his absence from Friday prayer, despite the proximity of his home? Give us a ruling, may you be rewarded.

He answered:

Rather, he must attend Friday prayer, delaying his arrival so that he can attend and pray while his ablution remains valid. If he cannot attend without passing wind, he should attend even if he passes wind, for that does him no harm. And Allah knows best.

عَمَّنْ بِهِ قُرُوحٌ فِي بَعْضِ أَعْضَاءِ الْوُضُوءِ وَيَخْرُجُ مِنْ تِلْكَ الْقُرُوحِ قَيْحٌ يَنْتَشِرُ عَلَى مَحَلِّ الْفَرْضِ فِي غَيْرِ مَوْضِعِ الْقُرُوحِ؛ وَلَا يُمْكِنُ إزَالَةُ ذَلِكَ إلَّا إذَا أَزَالَهُ عَنْ الْقُرُوحِ أَيْضًا وَهُوَ يَجِدُ الْمَشَقَّةَ فِي إزَالَتِهَا؛ وَالْأَطِبَّاءُ لَا يَرَوْنَ فِي إزَالَتِهَا مَضَرَّةً عَلَى صَاحِبِ هَذِهِ الْقُرُوحِ؛ غَيْرَ أَنَّهُ هُوَ يَجِدُ الْأَلَمَ وَالْمَشَقَّةَ فِي إزَالَةِ ذَلِكَ بِسَبَبِ تَكْرَارِ الْوُضُوءِ فَهَلْ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ إزَالَةُ ذَلِكَ لِيَصِلَ الْمَاءُ إلَى مَا تَسَتَّرَ مِنْ مَحَلِّ الْفَرْضِ وَإِنْ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مَشَقَّةٌ مَعَ غَلَبَةِ ظَنِّهِ بَعْدَ تِلْكَ الْقُرُوحِ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، إذَا كَانَتْ إزَالَتُهُ تُوجِبُ زِيَادَةَ الْمَرَضِ أَوْ تَأَخُّرَ الْبُرْءِ لَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ إزَالَتُهُ.
 وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ فِيهِ هَذَا وَلَا هَذَا أَزَالَهُ اللَّهُمَّ إلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ شَيْئًا يَسِيرًا مِنْ جِنْسِ الْوَسَخِ الَّذِي عَلَى الْعَيْنِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ:
 فَلَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ أَنْ يُزِيلَ ذَلِكَ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

About a person who has sores on some of the body parts washed during ablution. Pus seeps from these sores and spreads beyond them over the area that must be washed. He cannot remove it from that area without also removing it from the sores, which causes him hardship. Physicians do not consider its removal harmful to him, but he experiences pain and hardship from removing it repeatedly when performing ablution. Must he remove it so that water reaches the covered portions of the area that must be washed, even if this causes him hardship, given his strong expectation concerning what follows those sores—or is he not obliged to do so?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah. If removing it would worsen the illness or delay healing, he is not obliged to remove it.

If it would do neither, he must remove it—unless it is a small amount comparable to the discharge that collects around the eye or something similar. He is not obliged to remove that. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

About someone who holds that vomiting invalidates ablution and cites as evidence the report that the Prophet “once vomited and performed ablution.” He also relates another hadith: “He once vomited, washed his mouth, and said, ‘This is how ablution is performed after vomiting.’” Should one act upon the first hadith or the second?

He answered:

As for the second hadith, I have never heard of it. The first is in the Sunan collections, but its wording is:

“He vomited and broke his fast. This was mentioned to Thawbān, who said, ‘He spoke the truth; I poured out the water for his ablution.’”

Whenever the term “ablution” occurs in the Prophet’s speech, it means the ritual ablution prescribed by Islamic law. Its use to mean washing the hands and mouth occurs only in Jewish usage. It has been related that Salmān al-Fārisī said to the Prophet:

“We find in the Torah that ablution before a meal brings blessing to the food.” He replied, “Ablution before a meal and ablution after it bring blessing to the food.”

And Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ عَنْ الرُّعَافِ:
هَلْ يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
 إذَا تَوَضَّأَ مِنْهُ فَهُوَ أَفْضَلُ وَلَا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ فِي أَظْهَرِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ.
وَسُئِلَ:
هَلْ يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ النَّوْمُ جَالِسًا أَمْ لَا؟

 هَلْ يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِ الْوُضُوءُ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ،
 أَمَّا النَّوْمُ الْيَسِيرُ مِنْ الْمُتَمَكِّنِ بِمَقْعَدَتِهِ فَهَذَا لَا يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ عِنْدَ جَمَاهِيرِ الْعُلَمَاءِ مِنْ الْأَئِمَّةِ الْأَرْبَعَةِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ فَإِنَّ النَّوْمَ عِنْدَهُمْ لَيْسَ بِحَدَثِ فِي نَفْسِهِ لَكِنَّهُ مَظِنَّةُ الْحَدَثِ كَمَا دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ الْحَدِيثُ الَّذِي فِي السُّنَنِ:
 
{الْعَيْنُ وِكَاءُ السه فَإِذَا نَامَتْ الْعَيْنَانِ اسْتَطْلَقَ الْوِكَاءُ}
 وَفِي
translated_text:
He was asked about nosebleeds:

Do they invalidate ablution or not?

He answered:

It is preferable to perform ablution after a nosebleed, but it is not obligatory according to the stronger of the two scholarly opinions.

He was asked:

Does sleeping while seated invalidate ablution? If a man sits with his knees drawn up and held by his hands, then dozes off, his grip loosens, his hand falls to the ground, and he leans over without his side reaching the ground, must he perform ablution or not?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah.

Light sleep while seated with one’s buttocks firmly planted does not invalidate ablution according to the great majority of scholars, including the four imams and others. In their view, sleep is not itself a state of ritual impurity, but rather a circumstance in which ritual impurity may occur, as indicated by the hadith in the Sunan collections:

“The eye is the tie that keeps the anus closed; when both eyes sleep, the tie comes loose.”

And in

translated_text:
one narration:

“Whoever sleeps, let him perform ablution.”

This is also supported by the report in the two Sahīh collections that the Prophet:

“Would sleep until he was breathing heavily, then rise and pray without performing ablution.”

This was because his eyes would sleep but his heart would not; he remained aware. Had anything passed from him, he would have felt it. This shows that sleep is not itself a state of ritual impurity. If it were, there would be no distinction in this regard between the Prophet and anyone else, just as there is none regarding urination, defecation, and other causes of ritual impurity.

It is also established in the Sahīh collection that the Prophet:

“Would delay the night prayer until the Companions of Allah’s Messenger were nodding their heads; then they would pray without performing ablution.”

This shows that sleep as such does not invalidate ablution. If it did, their ablution would have been invalidated by this sleep in which their heads nodded.

Beyond this, scholars hold three views:

One view is that sleep in any position other than sitting invalidates ablution, without qualification. This is the view of Mālik and one view reported from Ahmad.

Another view is that sleeping while standing or sitting does not invalidate ablution, whereas sleeping while bowing or prostrating does;

A third view is that sleeping while standing, sitting, bowing, or prostrating does not invalidate ablution, unlike sleeping while lying down or in other positions. This is the view of Abū Hanīfa and the third view reported from Ahmad. Ahmad’s position, however, restricts this to light sleep.

Those who hold this view cite a hadith in the Sunan collections:

“Ablution is not required of one who sleeps standing, sitting, bowing, or prostrating, but it is required of one who sleeps lying down.”

For when a person sleeps lying down, his joints relax, allowing a bodily emission to escape. This is unlike standing, sitting, bowing, and prostrating, in which the limbs remain firm rather than relaxed, so there is no cause for anything to pass from the body. Moreover, sleep in these positions is ordinarily light, since a person would fall if he fell deeply asleep. There are two views concerning a seated person whose hands fall to the ground.

The stronger view in this matter is that if someone who has performed ablution is unsure whether his sleep was of a kind that invalidates it, his ablution is not deemed invalid. This is because his state of ritual purity is established with certainty and is not negated by doubt. And Allah knows best.

وَسُئِلَ:
هَلْ لَمْسُ كُلِّ ذَكَرٍ يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ مِنْ الْآدَمِيِّينَ وَالْحَيَوَانِ؟ وَهَلْ بَاطِنُ الْكَفِّ هُوَ مَا دُونَ بَاطِنِ الْأَصَابِعِ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
لَمْسُ فَرْجِ الْحَيَوَانِ غَيْرُ الْإِنْسَانِ لَا يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ حَيًّا وَلَا مَيِّتًا بِاتِّفَاقِ الْأَئِمَّةِ وَذَكَرَ بَعْضُ الْمُتَأَخِّرِينَ مِنْ أَصْحَابِ الشَّافِعِيِّ فِيهِ وَجْهَيْنِ. وَإِنَّمَا تَنَازَعُوا فِي مَسِّ فَرْجِ الْإِنْسَانِ خَاصَّةً. وَبَطْنُ الْكَفِّ يَتَنَاوَلُ الْبَاطِنَ كُلَّهُ بَطْنَ الرَّاحَةِ وَالْأَصَابِعِ.
 وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَقُولُ:
 لَا يَنْقُضُ بِحَالِ: كَأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَأَحْمَد فِي رِوَايَةٍ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رَجُلٍ وَقَعَتْ يَدُهُ بِبَاطِنِ كَفِّهِ وَأَصَابِعِهِ عَلَى ذَكَرِهِ:
 فَهَلْ يَنْتَقِضُ وُضُوؤُهُ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
إذَا لَمْ يَتَعَمَّدْ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَنْتَقِضْ وُضُوءُهُ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

“Does touching any penis, whether human or animal, invalidate ablution? And does ‘the inner surface of the hand’ mean the palm alone, excluding the inner surfaces of the fingers?”

He replied:

“Touching the private parts of a nonhuman animal, whether alive or dead, does not invalidate ablution, according to the unanimous agreement of the imams. Some later scholars of al-Shāfiʿī’s school mentioned two views on this. Their disagreement concerned only touching human private parts. ‘The inner surface of the hand’ includes its entire inner surface: both the palm and the fingers.

“Some hold that such touching does not invalidate ablution under any circumstances, such as Abū Hanīfa and, according to one report, Ahmad.”

He was asked:

“If a man’s palm and the inner surfaces of his fingers happen to touch his penis, does this invalidate his ablution?”

He replied:

“If he did not do so deliberately, his ablution is not invalidated.”

{أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ}
 وَفِي الْقِرَاءَةِ الْأُخْرَى: أَوْ لَمَسْتُمْ.
translated_text:
He was asked:

“If a man kisses or embraces his wife and emits pre-ejaculatory fluid, must he perform ablution?”

He replied:

“His ablution is invalidated by that. He need only perform ablution, but must also wash his penis and testicles.”

He was asked:

“Does touching women invalidate ablution?”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. The jurists hold three views on whether touching women invalidates ablution: two extremes and a middle position. The weakest is that touching invalidates ablution even without desire, provided that the person touched is someone who might arouse desire. This is al-Shāfiʿī’s view, based on the words of Allah Most High:

“Or you have touched women” (aw lāmastum al-nisā’).

In the other reading: aw lamastum (“or you have touched”).

original_text:
الْقَوْلُ الثَّانِي:
 أَنَّ اللَّمْسَ لَا يَنْقُضُ بِحَالِ وَإِنْ كَانَ لِشَهْوَةِ. كَقَوْلِ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَغَيْرِهِ. وَكِلَا الْقَوْلَيْنِ يَذْكُرُ رِوَايَةً عَنْ أَحْمَد؛
 لَكِنَّ ظَاهِرَ مَذْهَبِهِ كَمَذْهَبِ مَالِكٍ وَالْفُقَهَاءِ السَّبْعَةِ:
 أَنَّ اللَّمْسَ إنْ كَانَ لِشَهْوَةِ نَقَضَ وَإِلَّا فَلَا. وَلَيْسَ فِي الْمَسْأَلَةِ قَوْلٌ مُتَوَجِّهٌ إلَّا هَذَا الْقَوْلُ أَوْ الَّذِي قَبْلَهُ. فَأَمَّا تَعْلِيقُ النَّقْضِ بِمُجَرَّدِ اللَّمْسِ فَهَذَا خِلَافُ الْأُصُولِ وَخِلَافُ إجْمَاعِ الصَّحَابَةِ وَخِلَافُ الْآثَارِ. وَلَيْسَ مَعَ قَائِلِهِ نَصٌّ وَلَا قِيَاسٌ. فَإِنْ كَانَ اللَّمْسُ فِي قَوْله تَعَالَى أَوْ لَمَسْتُمْ النِّسَاءَ إذَا أُرِيدَ بِهِ اللَّمْسُ بِالْيَدِ وَالْقُبْلَةِ وَنَحْوُ ذَلِكَ - كَمَا قَالَهُ ابْنُ عُمَرَ وَغَيْرُهُ -: فَقَدْ عُلِمَ أَنَّهُ حَيْثُ ذُكِرَ مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ فِي الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ فَإِنَّمَا يُرَادُ بِهِ مَا كَانَ لِشَهْوَةِ مِثْلَ قَوْلِهِ فِي آيَةِ الِاعْتِكَافِ: 
{وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ}
 وَمُبَاشَرَةُ الْمُعْتَكِفِ لِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ لَا تَحْرُمُ عَلَيْهِ بِخِلَافِ الْمُبَاشَرَةِ لِشَهْوَةِ. وَكَذَلِكَ الْمُحْرِمُ - الَّذِي هُوَ أَشَدُّ - لَوْ بَاشَرَ الْمَرْأَةَ لِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ لَمْ يَحْرُمْ عَلَيْهِ وَلَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ بِهِ دَمٌ.
 وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ:
 
{ثُمَّ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ}
 وَقَوْلُهُ: 
{لَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيْكُمْ إنْ طَلَّقْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ مَا لَمْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ}
 فَإِنَّهُ لَوْ مَسَّهَا مَسِيسًا خَالِيًا مِنْ غَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ لَمْ يَجِبْ بِهِ عِدَّةٌ وَلَا يَسْتَقِرُّ بِهِ مَهْرٌ؛
 وَلَا تَنْتَشِرُ بِهِ حُرْمَةُ الْمُصَاهَرَةِ:
 بِاتِّفَاقِ الْعُلَمَاءِ بِخِلَافِ مَا لَوْ مَسَّ الْمَرْأَةَ لِشَهْوَةِ
translated_text:
The second view:

Touching does not invalidate ablution under any circumstances, even when accompanied by desire. This is the view of Abū Hanīfah and others. Both views are reported from Ahmad. However, the apparent position of his school, like that of Mālik and the seven jurists, is that touching invalidates ablution if accompanied by desire, but not otherwise. The only tenable positions on this issue are this view and the preceding one.

As for making mere touching invalidate ablution, this contradicts the established principles, the consensus of the Companions, and the transmitted reports. Those who hold this view have neither textual evidence nor analogical reasoning to support it. If “touching” in the words of Allah Most High, “Or you have touched women,” is understood to mean touching with the hand, kissing, and the like—as Ibn ‘Umar and others maintained—then it is known that wherever such expressions occur in the Quran and Sunnah, they refer only to contact accompanied by desire. An example is His statement in the verse concerning devotional retreat:

“And do not have relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques.”

Physical contact without desire is not forbidden to someone observing devotional retreat, unlike contact accompanied by desire. Likewise, someone in the consecrated state for pilgrimage—whose restrictions are stricter—would not be forbidden to touch a woman without desire, nor would doing so require an animal sacrifice.

The same applies to His words:

“Then divorce them before you have touched them,”

and His words:

“There is no blame upon you if you divorce women before you have touched them.”

For if he touches her without any desire, this does not require her to observe a waiting period, make the dower definitively due, or establish prohibitions of marriage through affinity, by agreement of the scholars—unlike the case where he touches a woman with desire

original_text:
وَلَمْ يَخْلُ بِهَا وَلَمْ يَطَأْهَا:
 فَفِي اسْتِقْرَارِ الْمَهْرِ بِذَلِكَ نِزَاعٌ مَعْرُوفٌ بَيْنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي مَذْهَبِ أَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِ.
 فَمَنْ زَعَمَ أَنَّ قَوْلَهُ:
 أَوْ لَمَسْتُمْ النِّسَاءَ يَتَنَاوَلُ اللَّمْسَ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ لِشَهْوَةِ فَقَدْ خَرَجَ عَنْ اللُّغَةِ الَّتِي جَاءَ بِهَا الْقُرْآنُ بَلْ وَعَنْ لُغَةِ النَّاسِ فِي عُرْفِهِمْ فَإِنَّهُ إذَا ذُكِرَ الْمَسُّ الَّذِي يُقْرَنُ فِيهِ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلِ وَالْمَرْأَةِ عُلِمَ أَنَّهُ مَسُّ الشَّهْوَةِ كَمَا أَنَّهُ إذَا ذُكِرَ الْوَطْءُ الْمَقْرُونُ بَيْنَ الرَّجُلِ وَالْمَرْأَةِ عُلِمَ أَنَّهُ الْوَطْءُ بِالْفَرْجِ لَا بِالْقَدَمِ.
 وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّهُ لَا يَقُولُ:
 إنَّ الْحُكْمَ مُعَلَّقٌ بِلَمْسِ النِّسَاءِ مُطْلَقًا؛ بَلْ بِصِنْفِ مِنْ النِّسَاءِ وَهُوَ مَا كَانَ مَظِنَّةَ الشَّهْوَةِ. فَأَمَّا مَسُّ مَنْ لَا يَكُونُ مَظِنَّةً - كَذَوَاتِ الْمَحَارِمِ وَالصَّغِيرَةِ - فَلَا يُنْقَضُ بِهَا. فَقَدْ تَرَكَ مَا ادَّعَاهُ مِنْ الظَّاهِرِ وَاشْتَرَطَ شَرْطًا لَا أَصْلَ لَهُ بِنَصِّ وَلَا قِيَاسٍ؛ فَإِنَّ الْأُصُولَ الْمَنْصُوصَةَ تُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ اللَّمْسِ لِشَهْوَةِ وَاللَّمْسِ لِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ لَا تُفَرِّقُ بَيْنَ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْمَلْمُوسُ مَظِنَّةَ الشَّهْوَةِ أَوْ لَا يَكُونَ وَهَذَا هُوَ الْمَسُّ الْمُؤَثِّرُ فِي الْعِبَادَاتِ كُلِّهَا؛
 كَالْإِحْرَامِ وَالِاعْتِكَافِ وَالصِّيَامِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ وَإِذَا كَانَ هَذَا الْقَوْلُ لَا يَدُلُّ عَلَيْهِ ظَاهِرُ اللَّفْظِ وَلَا الْقِيَاسُ:
 لَمْ يَكُنْ لَهُ أَصْلٌ فِي الشَّرْعِ. وَأَمَّا مَنْ عَلَّقَ النَّقْضَ بِالشَّهْوَةِ فَالظَّاهِرُ الْمَعْرُوفُ فِي مِثْلِ ذَلِكَ دَلِيلٌ
translated_text:
and has neither been alone with her nor had intercourse with her—there is a well-known disagreement among scholars within Ahmad’s school and elsewhere over whether this makes the dower definitively due.

Whoever claims that His words, “Or you have touched women,” encompass touching even without desire has departed from the language in which the Quran was revealed, and indeed from people’s customary usage. When touching is mentioned in connection with a man and a woman, it is understood to mean touching with desire. Likewise, when the term for intercourse—which can also mean treading—is used in connection with a man and a woman, it is understood to mean intercourse with the sexual organ, not treading with the foot.

Moreover, the proponent of this view does not say that the ruling applies to touching women without qualification. Rather, he restricts it to a particular category of women: those presumed to arouse desire. Touching someone not presumed to arouse desire—such as an unmarriageable female relative or a young girl—does not, according to him, invalidate ablution. He has thus abandoned the apparent meaning to which he claimed to adhere and introduced a condition with no basis in either a text or analogy. The principles expressly laid down in the texts distinguish between touching with desire and touching without desire; they do not distinguish according to whether the person touched is presumed to arouse desire. It is touching with desire that has legal consequences in all acts of worship, such as the consecrated state for pilgrimage, devotional retreat, fasting, and others.

Since this view is supported by neither the apparent meaning of the wording nor analogy, it has no basis in Islamic law. As for those who make the invalidation of ablution dependent on desire, the familiar, apparent meaning of such language provides evidence

original_text:
لَهُ؛ وَقِيَاسُ أُصُولِ الشَّرِيعَةِ دَلِيلٌ. وَمَنْ لَمْ يَجْعَلْ اللَّمْسَ نَاقِضًا بِحَالِ فَإِنَّهُ يَجْعَلُ اللَّمْسَ إنَّمَا أُرِيدَ بِهِ الْجِمَاعُ؛ كَمَا فِي قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{وَإِنْ طَلَّقْتُمُوهُنَّ مِنْ قَبْلِ أَنْ تَمَسُّوهُنَّ}
 وَنَظَائِرُهُ كَثِيرَةٌ.
 وَفِي السُّنَنِ:
 أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ 
{قَبَّلَ بَعْضَ نِسَائِهِ ثُمَّ صَلَّى وَلَمْ يَتَوَضَّأْ؛}
 لَكِنْ تُكُلِّمَ فِيهِ. وَأَيْضًا فَمِنْ الْمَعْلُومِ أَنَّ مَسَّ النَّاسِ نِسَاءَهُمْ مِمَّا تَعُمُّ بِهِ الْبَلْوَى وَلَا يَزَالُ الرَّجُلُ يَمَسُّ امْرَأَتَهُ؛ فَلَوْ كَانَ هَذَا مِمَّا يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ لَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ بَيَّنَهُ لِأُمَّتِهِ؛
 وَلَكَانَ مَشْهُورًا بَيْنَ الصَّحَابَةِ وَلَمْ يَنْقُلْ أَحَدٌ أَنَّ أَحَدًا مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ كَانَ يَتَوَضَّأُ بِمُجَرَّدِ مُلَاقَاةِ يَدِهِ لِامْرَأَتِهِ أَوْ غَيْرِهَا وَلَا نَقَلَ أَحَدٌ فِي ذَلِكَ حَدِيثًا عَنْ النَّبِيِّ:
 فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ قَوْلٌ بَاطِلٌ. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ مَسِّ النِّسَاءِ:
 هَلْ يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
فِيهِ ثَلَاثَةُ أَقْوَالٍ لِلْفُقَهَاءِ:
 أَحَدُهَا: أَنَّهُ لَا يَنْقُضُ بِحَالِ. كَقَوْلِ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَغَيْرِهِ.
translated_text:
for their view; analogy based on the principles of Islamic law also supports it. Those who hold that touching never invalidates ablution understand “touching” here to mean intercourse, as in the words of Allah Most High:

“If you divorce them before you have touched them.”

There are many similar examples.

The Sunan collections report that the Prophet “kissed one of his wives, then prayed without performing ablution.” However, the authenticity of this report has been questioned.

Moreover, it is well known that men touching their wives is an everyday occurrence: a man regularly touches his wife. Had this invalidated ablution, the Prophet would have explained it to his community, and it would have been well known among the Companions. Yet no one has reported that any Companion would perform ablution merely because his hand touched his wife or another woman, nor has anyone transmitted a hadith from the Prophet to that effect. It is thus clear that this view is false. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Does touching women invalidate ablution or not?

He answered:

The jurists hold three views on this:

First: It does not invalidate ablution under any circumstances. This is the view of Abū Hanīfa and others.

original_text:
وَالثَّانِي:
 أَنَّهُ إنْ كَانَ لَهُ شَهْوَةٌ نَقَضَ وَإِلَّا فَلَا. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ وَغَيْرِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
 وَالثَّالِثُ:
 يَنْقُضُ فِي الْجُمْلَةِ وَإِنْ لَمْ يَكُنْ بِشَهْوَةِ. وَهُوَ قَوْلُ الشَّافِعِيِّ وَغَيْرِهِ. وَعَنْ أَحْمَد بْنِ حَنْبَلٍ ثَلَاثُ رِوَايَاتٍ كَالْأَقْوَالِ الثَّلَاثَةِ لَكِنَّ الْمَشْهُورَ عَنْهُ قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ. وَالصَّحِيحُ فِي الْمَسْأَلَةِ أَحَدُ قَوْلَيْنِ؛ إمَّا الْأَوَّلُ وَهُوَ عَدَمُ النَّقْضِ مُطْلَقًا؛ وَإِمَّا الْقَوْلُ الثَّانِي وَهُوَ النَّقْضُ إذَا كَانَ بِشَهْوَةِ. وَأَمَّا وُجُوبُ الْوُضُوءِ مِنْ مُجَرَّدِ مَسِّ الْمَرْأَةِ لِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ فَهُوَ أَضْعَفُ الْأَقْوَالِ وَلَا يُعْرَفُ هَذَا الْقَوْلُ عَنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ وَلَا رَوَى أَحَدٌ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ أَنَّهُ أَمَرَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنْ يَتَوَضَّئُوا مِنْ ذَلِكَ؛ مَعَ أَنَّ هَذَا الْأَمْرَ غَالِبٌ لَا يَكَادُ يَسْلَمُ فِيهِ أَحَدٌ فِي عُمُومِ الْأَحْوَالِ؛ فَإِنَّ الرَّجُلَ لَا يَزَالُ يُنَاوِلُ امْرَأَتَهُ شَيْئًا وَتَأْخُذُهُ بِيَدِهَا وَأَمْثَالُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا يَكْثُرُ ابْتِلَاءُ النَّاسِ بِهِ فَلَوْ كَانَ الْوُضُوءُ مِنْ ذَلِكَ وَاجِبًا لَكَانَ النَّبِيُّ يَأْمُرُ بِذَلِكَ مَرَّةً بَعْدَ مَرَّةٍ وَيَشِيعُ ذَلِكَ وَلَوْ فَعَلَ لَنُقِلَ ذَلِكَ عَنْهُ وَلَوْ بِأَخْبَارِ الْآحَادِ فَلَمَّا لَمْ يَنْقُلْ عَنْهُ أَحَدٌ مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ أَنَّهُ أَمَرَ أَحَدًا مِنْ الْمُسْلِمِينَ بِشَيْءِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ - مَعَ عُمُومِ الْبَلْوَى بِهِ - عُلِمَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ غَيْرُ وَاجِبٍ
translated_text:
Second: It invalidates ablution if accompanied by sexual desire; otherwise, it does not. This is the view of Mālik and other scholars of Medina.

Third: It invalidates ablution in some circumstances even without sexual desire. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī and others. Three positions are reported from Ahmad ibn Hanbal, corresponding to these three views, but his best-known position agrees with Mālik’s.

The correct view on this matter is one of the first two: either touching does not invalidate ablution at all, or it invalidates it when accompanied by sexual desire. As for requiring ablution merely because one has touched a woman without sexual desire, this is the weakest view. It is not known to have been held by any of the Companions, nor has anyone reported that the Prophet instructed Muslims to perform ablution because of it.

Yet such contact is commonplace, and scarcely anyone avoids it in everyday life. A man regularly hands his wife something, which she takes in her hand, and similar situations arise frequently in people’s lives. Had ablution been obligatory because of this, the Prophet would have commanded it repeatedly, and it would have become widely known. Had he done so, it would have been transmitted from him, even if only through solitary reports. Since no Muslim has reported that he instructed any Muslim to do any such thing—despite everyone’s frequent exposure to it—it is clear that this is not obligatory.

original_text:
وَأَيْضًا فَلَوْ أَمَرَهُمْ بِذَلِكَ لَكَانُوا يَنْقُلُونَهُ وَيَأْمُرُونَ بِهِ. وَلَمْ يُنْقَلْ عَنْ أَحَدٍ مِنْ الصَّحَابَةِ أَنَّهُ أَمَرَ بِالْوُضُوءِ مِنْ مُجَرَّدِ الْمَسِّ الْعَارِي عَنْ شَهْوَةٍ بَلْ تَنَازَعَ الصَّحَابَةُ فِي قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{أَوْ لَامَسْتُمُ النِّسَاءَ}
 فَكَانَ ابْنُ عَبَّاسٍ وَطَائِفَةٌ يَقُولُونَ: الْجِمَاعُ وَيَقُولُونَ: اللَّهُ حَيِيٌّ كَرِيمٌ يُكَنِّي بِمَا يَشَاءُ عَمَّا شَاءَ. وَهَذَا أَصَحُّ الْقَوْلَيْنِ. وَقَدْ تَنَازَعَ عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنُ عُمَرَ وَالْعَرَبُ وَعَطَاءُ بْنُ أَبِي رَبَاحٍ وَالْمَوَالِي هَلْ الْمُرَادُ بِهِ الْجِمَاعُ أَوْ مَا دُونَهُ؟
 فَقَالَتْ الْعَرَبُ:
 هُوَ الْجِمَاعُ.
 وَقَالَتْ:
 الْمَوَالِي هُوَ مَا دُونَهُ. وَتَحَاكَمُوا إلَى ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ فَصَوَّبَ الْعَرَبَ وَخَطَّأَ الْمَوَالِيَ.
 وَكَانَ ابْنُ عُمَرَ يَقُولُ:
 قُبْلَةُ الرَّجُلِ امْرَأَتَهُ وَمَسُّهَا بِيَدِهِ مِنْ الْمُلَامَسَةِ وَهَذَا قَوْلُ مَالِكٍ وَغَيْرِهِ مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَدِينَةِ.
 وَمِنْ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَقُولُ:
 إنَّ هَذَا قَوْلُ ابْنِ عُمَرَ وَابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ؛ لِكَوْنِهِمَا كَانَا لَا يَرَيَانِ التَّيَمُّمَ لِلْجُنُبِ؛ فَيَتَأَوَّلَانِ الْآيَةَ عَلَى نَقْضِ الْوُضُوءِ. وَلَكِنْ قَدْ صُرِّحَ فِي الْآيَةِ أَنَّ الْجُنُبَ يَتَيَمَّمُ.
 وَقَدْ نَاظَرَ أَبُو مُوسَى ابْنَ مَسْعُودٍ بِالْآيَةِ فَلَمْ يُجِبْهُ ابْنُ مَسْعُودٍ بِشَيْءِ وَقَدْ ذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ الْبُخَارِيُّ فِي صَحِيحِهِ:
 فَعُلِمَ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ كَانَ مِنْ عَدَمِ اسْتِحْضَارِهِ لِمُوجَبِ الْآيَةِ.
translated_text:
Moreover, had he commanded them to do so, they would have transmitted that command and instructed others accordingly. Yet no Companion is reported to have required ablution merely for touching without sexual desire. Rather, the Companions differed over the meaning of the Most High’s words:

“Or you have touched women.”

Ibn ʿAbbās and a group of others said that this meant sexual intercourse. They would say: “Allah is Modest and Generous; He uses whatever euphemisms He wills for whatever He wills.” This is the more correct of the two views.

ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar, the Arabs, ʿAtāʾ ibn Abī Rabāh, and the mawālī (clients) disputed whether the phrase meant sexual intercourse or something short of it. The Arabs said, “It means sexual intercourse,” while the mawālī said, “It means something short of that.” They referred their dispute to Ibn ʿAbbās, who judged the Arabs correct and the mawālī mistaken.

Ibn ʿUmar used to say: “A man’s kissing his wife and touching her with his hand come under ‘touching.’” This is the view of Mālik and other scholars of Medina.

Some say that this was the view of Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn Masʿūd because neither considered dry ablution permissible for someone in a state of janābah (major ritual impurity). They therefore interpreted the verse as referring to what invalidates ablution. Yet the verse explicitly states that someone in a state of janābah may perform dry ablution.

Abū Mūsā cited the verse in his debate with Ibn Masʿūd, and Ibn Masʿūd gave him no answer. Al-Bukhārī recorded this in his Sahīh. It is thus clear that this was because he had not brought to mind what the verse entails.

original_text:
وَمَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ الصَّحَابَةَ الْأَكَابِرَ الَّذِينَ أَدْرَكُوا النَّبِيَّ لَوْ كَانُوا يَتَوَضَّؤُونَ مَنْ مَسِّ نِسَائِهِمْ مُطْلَقًا؛
 وَلَوْ كَانَ النَّبِيُّ أَمَرَهُمْ بِذَلِكَ:
 لَكَانَ هَذَا مِمَّا يَعْلَمُهُ بَعْضُ الصِّغَارِ؛
 كَابْنِ عُمَرَ وَابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَبَعْضُ التَّابِعِينَ فَإِذَا لَمْ يَنْقُلْ ذَلِكَ صَاحِبٌ وَلَا تَابِعٌ:
 كَانَ ذَلِكَ دَلِيلًا عَلَى أَنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمْ يَكُنْ مَعْرُوفًا بَيْنَهُمْ وَإِنَّمَا تَكَلَّمَ الْقَوْمُ فِي تَفْسِيرِ الْآيَةِ وَالْآيَةُ إنْ كَانَ الْمُرَادُ بِهَا الْجِمَاعَ فَلَا كَلَامَ وَإِنْ كَانَ أُرِيدَ بِهَا مَا هُوَ أَعَمُّ مِنْ الْجِمَاعِ فَيُقَالُ: حَيْثُ ذَكَرَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى فِي كِتَابِهِ مَسَّ النِّسَاءِ وَمُبَاشَرَتَهُنَّ وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ: فَلَا يُرِيدُ بِهِ إلَّا مَا كَانَ عَلَى وَجْهِ الشَّهْوَةِ وَاللَّذَّةِ وَأَمَّا اللَّمْسُ الْعَارِي عَنْ ذَلِكَ فَلَا يُعَلِّقُ اللَّهُ بِهِ حُكْمًا مِنْ الْأَحْكَامِ أَصْلًا وَهَذَا كَقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: 
{وَلَا تُبَاشِرُوهُنَّ وَأَنْتُمْ عَاكِفُونَ فِي الْمَسَاجِدِ}
 فَنَهَى الْعَاكِفَ عَنْ مُبَاشَرَةِ النِّسَاءِ مَعَ أَنَّ الْعُلَمَاءَ يَعْلَمُونَ أَنَّ الْمُعْتَكِفَ لَوْ مَسَّ امْرَأَتَهُ بِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ لَمْ يَحْرُمْ ذَلِكَ عَلَيْهِ وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي الصَّحِيحِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ 
{: أَنَّهُ كَانَ يُدْنِي رَأْسَهُ إلَى عَائِشَةَ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا فَتُرَجِّلُهُ وَهُوَ مُعْتَكِفٌ}
 وَمَعْلُومٌ أَنَّ ذَلِكَ مَظِنَّةُ مَسِّهِ لَهَا وَمَسِّهَا لَهُ. وَأَيْضًا فَالْإِحْرَامُ أَشَدُّ مِنْ الِاعْتِكَافِ وَلَوْ مَسَّتْهُ الْمَرْأَةُ لِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ لَمْ يَأْثَمْ بِذَلِكَ وَلَمْ يَجِبْ عَلَيْهِ دَمٌ.
 وَهَذَا الْوَجْهُ يُسْتَدَلُّ بِهِ مِنْ وَجْهَيْنِ:
 مِنْ جِهَةِ ظَاهِرِ الْخِطَابِ؛ وَمِنْ جِهَةِ الْمَعْنَى وَالِاعْتِبَارِ؛ فَإِنَّ خِطَابَ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى
translated_text:
And it is well known that if the senior Companions who knew the Prophet had performed ablution whenever they touched their wives, without qualification, and if the Prophet had commanded them to do so, some of the younger Companions, such as Ibn ʿUmar and Ibn ʿAbbās, and some of the Successors would have known about it. Since neither a Companion nor a Successor transmitted this, that is evidence that such a practice was not known among them. They were merely discussing the interpretation of the verse.

If the verse means sexual intercourse, there is nothing further to discuss. If it means something broader than sexual intercourse, then the answer is this: wherever Allah Most High mentions touching women, having intimate contact with them, or similar expressions in His Book, He means only what involves sexual desire and pleasure. As for touching devoid of that, Allah attaches no legal ruling whatsoever to it. This is illustrated by His words:

“And do not have intimate relations with them while you are in retreat in the mosques.”

He thus forbade someone observing devotional retreat from having intimate contact with women. Yet scholars know that if someone observing retreat touches his wife without sexual desire, this is not forbidden to him. It is established in the Sahīh concerning the Prophet:

“He would bring his head close to ʿĀ’ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, and she would comb his hair while he was observing devotional retreat.”

It is well known that this would be likely to involve his touching her and her touching him. Moreover, the restrictions of consecration for pilgrimage are stricter than those of devotional retreat. Yet if a woman touches a man in that state without sexual desire, he incurs no sin thereby, nor is he required to offer a sacrifice.

This argument provides evidence in two ways: through the apparent meaning of the wording, and through its underlying meaning and analogical reasoning. For the words of Allah Most High

original_text:
فِي الْقُرْآنِ بِذِكْرِ اللَّمْسِ وَالْمَسِّ وَالْمُبَاشَرَةِ لِلنِّسَاءِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ:

translated_text:
in the Quran that speak of touching women, physical contact with them, intimate relations with them, and the like do not encompass contact entirely devoid of sexual desire. Muslims have not disputed any of this except in the case of the verse on ablution, and that dispute arose only later. Thus, what they unanimously agreed upon must govern the matter disputed by their later generations.

As for analogical reasoning, Allah has attached no legal ruling to mere touching. He has neither made it entail any obligation nor forbidden it during any act of worship—whether devotional retreat, consecration for pilgrimage, prayer, fasting, or anything else. Nor has He made it establish marriage prohibitions arising from affinity or any other legal consequence. Rather, in Islamic law, it is like touching a woman through her clothing and other forms of contact that Allah has not made grounds for imposing any obligation or prohibition.

That being so, requiring ablution on account of such contact contradicts the established principles of Islamic law and what has been transmitted from the Companions. It is a position unsupported by either the Book or the Sunnah; indeed, what is known from the Sunnah contradicts it. This position is even weaker than that of those who regard semen as impure, for the view that semen is impure is itself weak. For if the Prophet did not command anyone to wash semen from his body or clothing, despite how frequently people were affected by this during his lifetime—yet commanded a menstruating woman to wash blood from her clothing, although this occurred far less frequently than semen soiling men—then, had such washing been obligatory, he would have made that clear. Rather, he would wash or wipe it off because he found it unpleasant,

كَمَا كَانَتْ عَائِشَةُ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهَا تَارَةً تَغْسِلُهُ وَتَارَةً تَفْرُكُهُ مِنْ ثَوْبِهِ.

 وَأَيْضًا فَإِيجَابُ الْوُضُوءِ مِنْ جِنْسِ اللَّمْسِ كَمَسِّ النِّسَاءِ وَمَسِّ الذَّكَرِ إنْ لَمْ يُعَلَّلْ بِكَوْنِهِ مَظِنَّةَ تَحْرِيكِ الشَّهْوَةِ وَإِلَّا كَانَ مُخَالِفًا لِلْأُصُولِ فَأَمَّا إذَا عُلِّلَ بِتَحْرِيكِ الشَّهْوَةِ كَانَ مُنَاسِبًا لِلْأُصُولِ وَهُنَا لِلْفُقَهَاءِ طَرِيقَانِ:
 أَحَدُهُمَا: قَوْلُ مَنْ يَقُولُ: إنَّ ذَلِكَ مَظِنَّةُ خُرُوجِ النَّاقِضِ فَأُقِيمَتْ الْمَظِنَّةُ مَقَامَ الْحَقِيقَةِ. وَهَذَا قَوْلٌ ضَعِيفٌ؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَظِنَّةَ إنَّمَا تُقَامُ مَقَامَ الْحَقِيقَةِ إذَا كَانَتْ الْحِكْمَةُ خَفِيَّةً وَكَانَتْ الْمَظِنَّةُ تُفْضِي إلَيْهَا غَالِبًا؛ وَكِلَاهُمَا مَعْدُومٌ؛ فَإِنَّ الْخَارِجَ لَوْ خَرَجَ لَعَلِمَ بِهِ الرَّجُلُ. وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّ مَسَّ الذَّكَرِ لَا يُوجِبُ خُرُوجَ شَيْءٍ فِي الْعَادَةِ أَصْلًا؛ فَإِنَّ الْمَنِيَّ إنَّمَا يَخْرُجُ بِالِاسْتِمْنَاءِ
translated_text:
just as ‘Ā’ishah—may Allah be pleased with her—would sometimes wash it off his garment and sometimes scrape it off.

Sa‘d ibn Abī Waqqās and Ibn ‘Abbās used to say: “Remove it from yourself, even with a sprig of idhkhir grass, for it is no different from mucus and saliva.” ‘Amra used to wash it from his garment. If he believed semen to be impure, then this is a disagreement among the Companions, and the Sunnah settles their disagreement. If the view that semen is impure has weak support in the Sunnah—since the Prophet did not command that it be washed off, despite how commonly people were affected by it—then this other view is weaker still. For none of the Companions reported that mere touching, entirely devoid of desire, invalidates ablution. They disagreed only about contact ordinarily associated with desire, such as kissing, squeezing with the hand, and the like.

Furthermore, requiring ablution because of touching, whether touching women or touching the penis, conflicts with the established principles unless its rationale is that such contact is likely to arouse desire. If, however, it is explained by the arousal of desire, it accords with those principles. Here the jurists take two approaches:

The first is the position of those who say that such contact makes the discharge of something that invalidates ablution likely, so the likelihood is treated as equivalent to its actual occurrence. This is a weak position. A circumstance indicating likelihood is treated as equivalent to actual occurrence only when the underlying reason for the ruling is not readily discernible and that circumstance usually leads to it. Neither condition is present here: if anything were discharged, the man would know it. Moreover, touching the penis does not ordinarily cause any discharge at all, for semen is emitted only when ejaculation is deliberately induced

{وَهَلْ هُوَ إلَّا بَضْعَةٌ مِنْك؟}
 وَحَمْلُ الْأَمْرُ عَلَى الِاسْتِحْبَابِ أَوْلَى مِنْ النَّسْخِ. وَكَذَلِكَ الْوُضُوءُ مِمَّا مَسَّتْ النَّارُ مُسْتَحَبٌّ فِي أَحَدِ الْقَوْلَيْنِ فِي
translated_text:
and that requires a full ritual bath. Pre-ejaculatory fluid is discharged following thoughts, looking, or touching a woman—not touching the penis. If they do not require ablution after looking, which is more likely to lead to the discharge of semen, then there is even less reason to require it after touching the penis.

The second position is that touching arouses desire, as when touching a woman, and ablution is performed following the arousal of desire, just as it is performed after anger or eating camel meat, because of Satan’s influence in these things, which ablution extinguishes. Hence, some followers of Abū Hanīfah said that ablution is required only when a strong erection occurs. Likewise, some followers of Mālik said that ablution is required when an erection occurs. But is this ablution after touching obligatory or recommended? The jurists disagree on this, and this is not the place to discuss it, for the question of touching the penis is discussed elsewhere. Our concern here is only the question of touching women.

The more evident view is also that ablution after touching the penis is recommended, not obligatory. Imam Ahmad explicitly stated this in one of the two opinions reported from him. This reconciles the hadiths and reports by understanding the command to perform ablution as a recommendation, without abrogating his saying:

“Is it not merely a part of you?”

Understanding the command as a recommendation is preferable to considering it abrogated. Likewise, ablution after eating food cooked over fire is recommended according to one of the two views in

 . وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ الرَّجُلِ يَمَسُّ الْمَرْأَةَ:
 هَلْ يَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ أَمْ لَا؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
إنْ تَوَضَّأَ مِنْ ذَلِكَ الْمَسِّ فَحَسَنٌ وَإِنْ صَلَّى وَلَمْ يَتَوَضَّأْ صَحَّتْ صَلَاتُهُ فِي أَظْهَرِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ.
translated_text:
the schools of Ahmad and other scholars. This reconciles his command to perform ablution with his refraining from it. As for abrogation, there is no evidence for it; rather, the evidence indicates the contrary.

Likewise, ablution following the discharge of impurities from elsewhere in the body, rather than the two natural outlets—such as after vomiting, nosebleeds, cupping, venesection, or wounds—is recommended, as reports relate that the Prophet and the Companions performed ablution after these things. As for making it obligatory, nothing in the Quran or Sunnah establishes such an obligation.

Similarly, ablution after loud laughter is recommended according to one of the two views in Ahmad’s school. The reported hadith commanding those who laughed aloud to perform ablution is understood as follows: they had sinned by laughing, and it is recommended for anyone who commits a sin to perform ablution and pray two units of prayer. As related in the Sunan collections, Abū Bakr reported that the Prophet said:

“No Muslim commits a sin, then performs ablution, prays two units of prayer, and seeks Allah’s forgiveness, without Allah forgiving him.”

And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

“Does a man’s touching a woman invalidate his ablution or not?”

He replied:

“If he performs ablution after that touch, that is good. But if he prays without performing ablution, his prayer is valid according to the more evident of the two scholarly views.”

translated_text:
Shaykh al-Islām—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked: (*)

“If a man touches the hand of a beardless youth, is this treated like touching a woman with regard to invalidating ablution? What has been reported concerning the prohibition of looking at the face of a handsome beardless youth? And what of the claim made by some who contravene Islamic law that looking at a beardless youth’s face is an act of worship? When someone tells them, ‘Looking in this way is forbidden,’ one of them replies, ‘When I look at him, I say: Glory be to the One who created him. I add nothing to that.’”

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If a man touches a beardless youth with desire, there are two views within the school of Ahmad and among other scholars.

The first is that, like touching a woman with desire, it invalidates ablution. This is the well-known position in Mālik’s school, as mentioned by al-Qādī Abū Yaʿlā in his exposition of the school.

The second is that it does not invalidate ablution. This is the well-known position in al-Shāfiʿī’s school.

The first view is more evident, for anal intercourse invalidates the acts of worship that vaginal intercourse invalidates—such as fasting, the consecrated state of pilgrimage, and devotional retreat—and requires a full ritual bath
translated_footnote:
Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd said (p. 174):
Several points should be noted:
First: This fatwa has already appeared at 15/410–427.
Second: The copy from which the fatwa is reproduced here differs from the copy used there, as the differences between them demonstrate. The copy used here is more accurate.
Third: There are some textual corruptions and omissions here, including the following:

1 - 21/243: “The first is that, like touching women with desire, it invalidates ablution. This is the well-known position in Mālik’s school, mentioned by al-Qādī Abū Ya‘lā in his exposition of the school’s doctrine.”
The following words have been omitted after this: “It is also one of the two positions within al-Shāfi‘ī’s school,” as found at 15/411.

2 - 21/248: “That is not because, in his view, it indicated the Creator’s greatness.” The more likely reading is: “That is not because it is more indicative,” as found at 15/416.

3 - 21/250: “On this basis, [the gaze] of someone whose heart feels no attraction to beardless youths.” The bracketed words have been omitted, as shown at 15/418.

4 - 21/253: “Then looking reinforces love.” The more likely reading is: “Then looking engenders love,” as found at 15/421.

5 - 21/253: “This afflicts only those who turn away from sincere devotion to Allah, as the Exalted says concerning Joseph: ‘Thus We acted to turn evil and indecency away from him; indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants.’” After “sincere devotion to Allah,” the following has been omitted: “who have some element of shirk (associating partners with Allah). As for those sincerely devoted to Him, however, it is as the Exalted says…” This appears at 15/421.

6 - 21/254: “and for the beloved, some healing in his affairs.” The correct wording is: “or for the beloved, some effort to further his interests,” as found at 15/422.

7 - 21/255: “which entails the indwelling of His very essence in His creatures or His union with them; [thus they say] concerning all creatures something analogous to what the Christians say specifically concerning Christ.” The bracketed words have been omitted, as shown at 15/423.

 فَإِنْ وَطِئَ فِي الدُّبُرِ تَعَلَّقَ بِهِ مَا ذُكِرَ مِنْ الْأَحْكَامِ وَإِنْ كَانَ الدُّبُرُ لَمْ يُخْلَقْ مَحَلًّا لِلْوَطْءِ مَعَ أَنَّ نُفْرَةَ الطِّبَاعِ عَنْ الْوَطْءِ فِي الدُّبُرِ أَعْظَمُ مَنْ نُفْرَتِهَا عَنْ الْمُلَامَسَةِ وَنَقْضُ الْوُضُوءِ بِالْمَسِّ يُرَاعَى فِيهِ حَقِيقَةُ الْحِكْمَةِ وَهُوَ أَنْ يَكُونَ الْمَسُّ لِشَهْوَةِ عِنْدَ الْأَكْثَرِينَ:
 كَمَالِكِ وَأَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِمَا كَمَا يُرَاعَى مِثْلُ ذَلِكَ فِي الْإِحْرَامِ وَالِاعْتِكَافِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ.

 فَكَذَلِكَ الْأَمْرَدُ.
 وَأَمَّا الشَّافِعِيُّ وَأَحْمَد فِي رِوَايَةٍ فَيَعْتَبِرُ الْمَظِنَّةَ وَهُوَ:
 أَنَّ النِّسَاءَ مَظِنَّةُ الشَّهْوَةِ فَيَنْقُضُ الْوُضُوءَ سَوَاءٌ بِشَهْوَةِ أَوْ بِغَيْرِ شَهْوَةٍ وَلِهَذَا لَا يَنْقُضُ لَمْسُ الْمَحَارِمِ لَكِنْ لَوْ لَمَسَ ذَوَاتِ مَحَارِمِهِ لِشَهْوَةِ فَقَدْ وُجِدَتْ حَقِيقَةُ الْحِكْمَةِ؛ وَكَذَلِكَ إذَا مَسَّ الْأَمْرَدَ لِشَهْوَةِ.
translated_text:
just as vaginal intercourse does. Thus, in matters of worship, the acts preliminary to either are treated alike. If someone touches a beardless youth with desire while in the consecrated state of pilgrimage, he must offer a sacrificial animal, just as he would if he touched a woman whom he is not forbidden to marry with desire. Likewise, touching him with desire must be treated like touching a woman with desire in terms of invalidating ablution.

Those who hold that touching him does not invalidate ablution argue: “He was not created for that purpose.” The response is: There is no doubt that he was not created for that purpose, and that sodomy is among the gravest forbidden acts. Yet this consideration does not determine the rulings on intercourse: anal intercourse entails the rulings already mentioned, even though the anus was not created for intercourse. Moreover, human nature’s aversion to anal intercourse is greater than its aversion to touching.

According to most scholars, including Mālik, Ahmad, and others, the invalidation of ablution through touching depends on whether the underlying rationale is actually present—namely, whether the touching involves desire. The same consideration applies to the consecrated state of pilgrimage, devotional retreat, and other matters. According to this view, wherever touching with desire occurs, the ruling applies. Even if someone touches his mother, sister, or daughter with desire, his ablution is invalidated. The same therefore applies to a beardless youth.

Al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad according to one reported view, instead take account of the presumed likelihood of desire: women are likely to arouse desire, so touching them invalidates ablution, whether with or without desire. This is why touching female relatives whom one is permanently forbidden to marry does not invalidate ablution. Yet if someone touches such a female relative with desire, the underlying rationale is actually present; the same applies if he touches a beardless youth with desire.

 وَقَوْلُ الْقَائِلِ:
 إنَّ النَّظَرَ إلَى وَجْهِ الْأَمْرَدِ عِبَادَةٌ كَقَوْلِهِ: إنَّ النَّظَرَ إلَى وُجُوهِ النِّسَاءِ أَوْ النَّظَرِ إلَى وُجُوهِ مَحَارِمِ الرَّجُلِ - كَبِنْتِ الرَّجُلِ
translated_text:
And taking sensual pleasure in touching a beardless youth, whether by shaking his hand or otherwise, is forbidden by the consensus of the Muslims, just as taking sensual pleasure in touching one’s female relatives whom one is permanently forbidden to marry, or a woman whom one is not forbidden to marry, is forbidden. Indeed, most scholars hold that this is a graver sin than taking sensual pleasure with a woman whom one is not forbidden to marry. Likewise, the majority hold that the punishment for sodomy is more severe than the punishment for unlawful intercourse with such a woman. Both the active and passive participants must therefore be put to death, whether either has muhsan status or not, and whether either is owned as a slave by the other or not. This is reported from the Prophet in the Sunan collections, and his Companions acted upon it without any known disagreement among them. The execution is by stoning, just as Allah destroyed the people of Lot by stoning. This is also the punishment prescribed by Islamic law when someone guilty of unlawful intercourse is to be executed: that person is stoned. Thus, the Prophet had Māʿiz ibn Mālik, the Ghāmidī woman, and the Jewish couple stoned, as well as the woman to whom he sent Unays, saying:

“Go to this man’s wife. If she confesses, stone her.”

She confessed, and he stoned her.

Looking with desire at the face of a beardless youth is like looking with desire at the face of a female relative whom one is permanently forbidden to marry or a woman whom one is not forbidden to marry. This applies whether the desire is for intercourse or for the pleasure of looking. If someone were to look at his mother, sister, or daughter, taking pleasure in looking at her as he takes pleasure in looking at the face of a woman whom he is not forbidden to marry, everyone would know that this is forbidden. The same applies to looking at the face of a beardless youth, by agreement of the imams.

To say that looking at the face of a beardless youth is an act of worship is like saying that looking at women’s faces, or at the faces of a man’s female relatives whom he is permanently forbidden to marry—such as a man’s daughter

and his mother and sister—is an act of worship. It is well known that whoever makes such forbidden looking an act of worship is like someone who makes indecencies acts of worship. Allah Most High says:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing this, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’”

It is also well known that the physical appearance of women whom a man is not forbidden to marry, and of his female relatives whom he is permanently forbidden to marry, may offer lessons and indications of the Creator of the same kind as those found in the appearance of beardless youths. Would any Muslim, then, say that a person may look in this manner at the appearance of women throughout the world and of his own female relatives whom he is permanently forbidden to marry, and claim that this is worship? Rather, whoever makes such looking an act of worship is a disbeliever and an apostate who must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is to be put to death. He is like someone who makes assisting a person seeking indecency an act of worship, or makes drinking a small quantity of wine an act of worship, or makes becoming intoxicated with hashish an act of worship.

Whoever makes assisting indecency, through procuring or otherwise, an act of worship, or makes anything he knows to be forbidden in the religion of Islam an act of worship, must be called upon to repent; if he does not repent, he is to be put to death. He resembles the polytheists of whom Allah says:

“When they commit an indecency, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing this, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say, ‘Allah does not command indecency. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?’”

Their indecency consisted only in circumambulating the House naked. They used to say, “We will not circumambulate in clothes in which we have disobeyed Allah.” Thus, they circumambulated naked only to avoid wearing clothes in which they had sinned, yet the foregoing was said of them. What, then, of someone who makes indecency involving sexual desire an act of worship?

translated_text:
Allah, Glorified is He, has commanded in His Book that the gaze be lowered. This is of two kinds: averting one’s gaze from nakedness, and averting it from objects of desire. The first includes a man averting his gaze from another person’s nakedness, as the Prophet said:

“A man must not look at another man’s nakedness, nor a woman at another woman’s nakedness.”

A person must also cover his own nakedness, as the Prophet said to Mu‘āwiyah ibn Haydah:

“Keep your nakedness covered, except from your wife or those whom your right hand possesses.”

I asked, “What if one of us is among his people?”

He replied, “If you can keep anyone from seeing it, then let no one see it.”

I asked, “What if one of us is alone?”

He replied, “Allah is more deserving than people of your modesty before Him.”

One may uncover oneself to the extent necessary, as when relieving oneself. Likewise, when a man bathes alone beside something that screens him, he may bathe naked, as Moses and Job did, and as in the accounts of the Prophet’s bathing on the day of the Conquest and his bathing in the hadith of Maymūnah.

As for the second kind of looking—such as looking at the concealed adornment of a woman whom one is not forbidden to marry—it is graver than the first, just as consuming wine is graver than consuming carrion, blood, or pork. The drinker of wine is liable to the prescribed punishment, whereas someone who consumes those other forbidden things without regarding them as lawful is liable to discretionary punishment. This is because people do not crave those forbidden things as they crave wine. Likewise, looking at a man’s nakedness is not desired in the way that looking at

women and the like is. Likewise, looking lustfully at a beardless youth falls into this category. Scholars unanimously agree that this is forbidden, just as they unanimously agree that looking lustfully at a woman whom one may marry, or at female relatives whom one is permanently forbidden to marry, is forbidden.

The Creator, glorified is He, is to be glorified upon seeing any of His creatures. Creating a beardless youth is no greater a marvel of His power than creating a bearded man, nor is creating women any greater a marvel of His power than creating men. Rather, singling out the sight of a beardless youth, but not others, as an occasion for glorifying Allah is like doing so at the sight of a woman but not a man. This is not because what he sees points him to the Creator’s greatness, but because beauty unsettles his heart and mind. What he sees may overwhelm him, so that his glorification is prompted by the desire aroused within him. Similarly, when the women saw Joseph,

“they were awestruck by him and cut their hands, and said, ‘Allah forbid! This is no human being; this is nothing but a noble angel.’”

It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet said:

“Allah does not look at your appearance or your wealth; rather, He looks at your hearts and your deeds.”

If Allah does not look at appearances or wealth, but rather at hearts and deeds, how can a person be deemed superior on grounds by which Allah has not deemed him superior?

The Most High said:

“Do not let your eyes long for what We have given some groups among them to enjoy—the splendour of this worldly life.”

And He said of the hypocrites:

“When you see them, their bodies impress you, and when they speak, you listen to what they say. They are like propped-up timbers. They think every cry is directed against them

If Allah has said what He has said about these hypocrites, whose bodies impress the beholder because of their splendour, comeliness and outward adornment—although they are not people looked at with lust—then what of those who are looked at with lust?

A person may be regarded for his faith and piety; here, what matters is his heart and deeds, not his appearance. He may also be looked at because his form points to the One who fashioned him, and this is good.

Or he may be looked at out of admiration for his physical beauty, just as one looks at a mountain, animals or trees. If this is done in the spirit of admiring worldly life, status and wealth, it too is blameworthy, for the Most High says:

“Do not let your eyes long for what We have given some groups among them to enjoy—the splendour of this worldly life, through which We test them.”

But if it is done in a way that does not diminish one’s religious commitment and merely refreshes the soul—as looking at flowers does—then it belongs to those idle diversions that help one pursue what is right.

Whenever any of these kinds of looking is accompanied by lust, it is undoubtedly forbidden, whether the desire is to take pleasure in a lustful gaze or to engage in sexual intercourse. There is a difference between what a person feels when looking at trees and flowers and what he feels when looking at women and beardless youths. Because of this distinction, the religious ruling differs. Looking at beardless youths thus falls into three categories:

original_text:

 كَذَلِكَ.
 وَإِنَّمَا وَقَعَ النِّزَاعُ بَيْنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي الْقِسْمِ الثَّالِثِ مِنْ النَّظَرِ وَهُوَ:
translated_text:
The first is looking accompanied by lust; this is forbidden by consensus.

The second is looking that is known with certainty to involve no lust, such as a devout man looking at his handsome son, his beautiful daughter or his mother. Such looking is not accompanied by lust unless the man is among the most depraved of people. Whenever lust accompanies it, it becomes forbidden.

The same applies to those whose hearts feel no attraction towards beardless youths—as was the case with the Companions, and with peoples unfamiliar with this indecency. Such a person makes no distinction between looking at such a face and looking at his own son, his neighbour’s son or an unrelated boy. No lustful thought enters his heart, because he has not become accustomed to this and his heart is free of such inclinations.

In the time of the Companions, slave women would walk in the streets with their heads uncovered and serve men, while people’s hearts were free of such desires. Yet if a man were to allow beautiful Turkish slave women to walk among people in places and times such as these, just as those slave women used to walk, this would be a form of corruption.

Likewise, handsome beardless youths should not go out, except as needed, in places and at times where there is a fear that they will become a source of temptation. A handsome beardless youth should therefore not be allowed to flaunt his beauty, sit in the bathhouse among unrelated men, dance among men, or do similar things that tempt people. The same applies to looking at him.

The scholars’ disagreement concerns only the third category of looking, namely:

looking at him without lust, but with fear that it may be aroused?

There are two views on this within Ahmad’s school. The sounder of them—which is also reported as al-Shāfi‘ī’s explicit position—is that it is impermissible. The second is that it is permissible, because the presumption is that lust will not be aroused; mere doubt therefore does not make it forbidden, though it may be disliked.

The first view is stronger. Likewise, the stronger view within the schools of al-Shāfi‘ī and Ahmad is that looking at the face of an unrelated woman without a need is impermissible, even in the absence of lust, because of the fear that it may be aroused. This is also why being alone with an unrelated woman is forbidden: it is a likely occasion for temptation. The general principle is that anything that causes temptation is impermissible, for the means leading to corruption must be blocked unless outweighed by a greater benefit. Thus, looking that leads to temptation is forbidden unless it serves an overriding benefit, as when a suitor, physician or someone else looks for such a purpose. Looking is permitted when needed, but without lust. As for looking without a need at someone who is a source of temptation, this is impermissible.

Anyone who repeatedly looks at a beardless youth or someone similar, or prolongs his gaze, and says, “I am not looking out of lust,” is lying. If there is no reason that makes looking necessary, he looks only because of the pleasure it brings to his heart.

An unintentional glance, however, is pardoned if he turns his gaze away, as established in the Sahīh, where Jarīr said: “I asked the Messenger of Allah about an unintentional glance, and he said:

translated_text:
‘Turn your gaze away.’” In the Sunan, it is reported that he said to ‘Alī: “O ‘Alī, do not follow one glance with another. The first is yours, but the second is not.”

In the hadith recorded in the Musnad and elsewhere:

“The gaze is a poisoned arrow from the arrows of Satan.”

It also states:

“Whoever looks at a woman’s beauty and then lowers his gaze from her, Allah will bestow upon his heart a sweetness of worship that he will experience until the Day of Resurrection”—or words to that effect.

For this reason, it is said that lowering one’s gaze from those whom one is forbidden to look at—such as a woman or a handsome beardless youth—brings three benefits of immense worth.

The first is the sweetness and delight of faith, which are sweeter and more pleasant than what one has given up for Allah. Whoever gives something up for Allah, Allah replaces it with something better. The soul loves to gaze upon such beauty, especially the souls of those devoted to spiritual discipline and purity. A tenderness remains within them that draws them to such beauty, until it continually draws one of them in and strikes him down as a beast of prey would.

For this reason, one of the Successors said: “I am no more fearful for a repentant young man when a beast of prey sits beside him than when a handsome youth sits beside him.” Another said: “Beware of looking at the sons of kings, for they present a temptation like that of virgins.”

The leading authorities in knowledge and religion—such as teachers of guidance and masters of the spiritual path—have always counselled against keeping company with youths. Indeed, it is related that Fath al-Mawsilī said:

“I kept company with thirty of the abdāl, each of whom, when parting from me, advised me not to keep company with youths.” One of them said: “No servant falls from Allah’s favour except through keeping company with these foul ones.”

Gazing then strengthens love, which becomes attachment, as the heart attaches itself to the beloved; then ardent longing, as the heart pours itself towards the beloved; then clinging passion, which holds fast to the heart like a creditor who never leaves his debtor; then passionate love, until it becomes utter enslavement. The word mutayyam means “enslaved”, and Taym Allāh means “servant of Allah”. The heart thus becomes the slave of someone unfit to be a brother, or even a servant. This afflicts only those who turn away from sincere devotion to Allah, as the Most High said concerning Joseph:

“Thus We turned evil and immorality away from him. Indeed, he was one of Our chosen servants.”

The wife of al-ʿAzīz was a polytheist, and despite being married, she fell into the evil she committed. Joseph, however, was protected by Allah through his sincere devotion to Him, despite being unmarried, despite her attempts to seduce him and her enlistment of the women’s help against him, and despite her punishing him with imprisonment for remaining chaste. This fulfilled the words He relates:

“I will surely mislead them all, except Your chosen servants among them.”

The Most High said:

“Indeed, you will have no authority over My servants, except those of the wayward who follow you.”

Waywardness means following one’s desires, and this matter is among the greatest avenues of following desires. Those who advocate passionate love for beautiful forms—whether philosophers such as Ibn Sīnā and his like, Persians, as is related of some of them, or ignorant Sufis—are people of misguidance and waywardness. Besides sharing in the Jews’ waywardness and the Christians’ misguidance, they have surpassed both communities in this regard. For

this—even if it is thought to benefit the lover by freeing his soul and refining his character, or the beloved through efforts to further his interests, educate him and cultivate his manners, and so forth—does far more harm than good. How could its benefit compare with its sin?

This is merely like saying that illicit intercourse benefits both parties through the pleasure and delight it brings, as well as the payment and other benefits the woman receives; or saying that drinking wine has physical and psychological benefits. Yet He said concerning wine and gambling:

“Say: In them is great sin and benefit for people, but their sin is greater than their benefit.”

This was before their prohibition, let alone what He said when prohibiting them and afterwards.

Attachment to beautiful forms belongs to the category of sexual immorality. Its hidden aspect is hidden sexual immorality and inward sin. The Most High said:

“Abandon both outward and inward sin.”

The Most High also said:

“Say: My Lord has only forbidden immoral deeds, whether committed openly or secretly.”

He also said:

“When they commit an immoral deed, they say, ‘We found our forefathers doing it, and Allah has commanded us to do it.’ Say: Allah does not command immorality. Do you say about Allah what you do not know?”

The leading scholars of the religion do not dispute that this is neither recommended nor obligatory. Whoever considers it praiseworthy and commends it has departed from the consensus of the Muslims—indeed, of the Jews and Christians as well—and even from the judgement of rational people among all nations. Such a person follows his desires without guidance from Allah:

“And who is more astray than one who follows his desires without guidance from Allah? Indeed, Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.”

He has also said

—exalted is He:

“But as for the one who feared standing before his Lord and restrained himself from desire, Paradise will indeed be his refuge.”

The Most High also said:

“Do not follow desire, lest it lead you astray from Allah’s path. Indeed, those who stray from Allah’s path will suffer a severe punishment because they forgot the Day of Reckoning.”

As for someone who gazes at beardless youths, imagining that he is gazing at divine beauty, and makes this a path to Allah—as various groups claiming knowledge of Allah do—his assertion constitutes greater disbelief than the assertions of idolaters and the disbelief of Lot’s people. Such people are among the worst apostate heretics, who must be put to death according to the unanimous consensus of the entire Muslim community. For the idolaters said:

“We worship them only so that they may bring us nearer to Allah.”

These people, however, hold that Allah exists within the idols themselves and dwells in them. By His appearance and manifestation in created things, they do not mean that these things point to Him and serve as signs for them. Rather, they mean that He Himself—glory be to Him—has appeared and manifested Himself in them. They liken this to the appearance of water in a glass bottle, butter in milk, oil in olives, oil in sesame seeds, and similar things that imply the indwelling of His very Essence in His creation or His union with it. They extend this to all created things, just as the Christians say it of Christ alone.

They regard beardless youths as manifestations of beauty, and establish this supreme form of associating partners with Allah as a means of declaring sexual immoralities lawful—indeed, of declaring everything forbidden lawful. Thus, the most distinguished of their later figures, al-Tilimsānī, was asked: “If your assertion that existence is one is true, what is the difference between my mother and my sister

and my daughter, such that one is lawful and another forbidden?” He replied: “To us, they are all alike. But those who are veiled said, ‘Forbidden,’ so we said, ‘Forbidden to you.’”

Among these adherents of divine indwelling and union are those who restrict indwelling and union to particular individuals: certain prophets, such as Christ; certain Companions, as the extremists claim concerning ʿAlī; certain spiritual masters, as the followers of al-Hallāj and others like them claim; certain kings; or certain bodily forms, such as those of beardless youths. One of them says: “I gaze upon my Creator’s attributes and behold them in this form.”

The disbelief in this statement is too plain to escape anyone who believes in Allah and His Messenger. If someone said such a thing about a noble prophet, he would be a disbeliever—so what if he says it about a beardless boy? May Allah disgrace a group whose object of worship is of the same kind as those with whom they have intercourse. The Most High has said:

“Nor would he order you to take the angels and prophets as lords. Would he order you to disbelieve after you had become Muslims?”

If those who take the angels and prophets as lords are disbelievers, even while acknowledging that they are Allah’s creatures, then what of those who take certain created beings as lords while claiming that Allah dwells within them or is united with them, that their existence is His existence, and other such assertions?

As for the second benefit of lowering the gaze, it brings illumination to the heart and grants discernment. The Most High said concerning Lot’s people:

“By your life, they were indeed wandering blindly in their intoxication.”

Two intoxications:

And it has been said:

They said, “Have you gone mad over the one you love?” I replied,
“Love is worse than what afflicts the mad.
The lover never regains his senses,
Whereas madness seizes its sufferer only from time to time.”

Allah, glorified be He, mentioned the verse of light immediately after the verses on lowering the gaze, saying:

“Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth.”

Shāh ibn Shujāʿ al-Kirmānī was never mistaken in his discernment. The third benefit is strength, steadfastness, and courage of heart. Allah grants him the power to prevail alongside the power of proof. A transmitted saying states:

“Satan fears even the shadow of one who resists his own desires.”

Thus, whoever follows his desires suffers the humiliation—abasement, weakness, and degradation of the soul—that Allah has appointed for those who disobey Him. For Allah has granted honour to those who obey Him and humiliation to those who disobey Him. The Most High says:

“They say, ‘If we return to Medina, the more honourable will surely expel the more humble from it.’ Yet honour belongs to Allah, His Messenger, and the believers.”

And the Most High says:

“Do not weaken or grieve, for you will have the upper hand, if you are believers.”

Hence the saying of the spiritual masters: “People seek honour at the gates of kings, but find it only in obedience to Allah.”

Al-Hasan al-Basrī used to say: “Though horses carry them at a graceful pace and mules clatter beneath them, the humiliation of disobedience hangs about their necks. Allah will not allow those who disobey Him to escape humiliation.”

Whoever obeys Allah has shown allegiance to Him in that obedience; whoever disobeys Him shares, to that extent, in the conduct of those who oppose Him through their sins. The qunūt supplication states:

“Indeed, none whom You befriend is humiliated, and none whom You oppose is honoured.”
