 أَنَّهُ مُسْتَحِيلٌ عَنْ الدَّمِ؛ لِأَنَّهُ دَمٌ قَصَرَتْهُ الشَّهْوَةُ وَلِهَذَا يَخْرُجُ عِنْدَ الْإِكْثَارِ مِنْ الْجِمَاعِ أَحْمَرَ وَالدَّمُ نَجِسٌ وَالنَّجَاسَةُ لَا تَطْهُرُ بِالِاسْتِحَالَةِ عِنْدَكُمْ.
translated_text:
impure, for removing it and clearing it away is less burdensome than purifying oneself on its account. If the more burdensome obligation is required, the lighter one is all the more warranted. This applies especially according to those who hold that the private parts must be cleansed after its discharge, since such cleansing consists of removing it and clearing it away. If removing it from its point of discharge is obligatory, removing it from elsewhere is even more warranted.

The third argument:

It belongs to the same category as pre-ejaculatory fluid and is therefore impure, like that fluid. Pre-ejaculatory fluid emerges during the initial stages of sexual arousal, whereas semen—the source of that fluid—emerges when arousal reaches its fullness. It passes through the same channel and emerges from the same opening. If the derivative is deemed impure, then its source is all the more deserving of that ruling.

The fourth argument:

It is discharged from the penis, or from the front passage, and is therefore impure, like all other discharges, such as urine, pre-ejaculatory fluid, and post-urinary discharge. This is because the ruling of impurity depends on the outlet. Do you not see that waste substances discharged from the upper parts of the body are not impure, whereas those discharged from its lower parts are impure, even though both undergo transformation within the body?

The fifth argument:

It is transformed blood, for it is blood that sexual desire has bleached. This is why it emerges red when intercourse is frequent. Blood is impure, and, according to you, an impure substance does not become pure through transformation.

الْوَجْهُ السَّادِسُ:

 فَهَذِهِ الطَّهَارَةُ إنْ قِيلَ:
 بِوُجُوبِهَا فَهِيَ مِنْ الْقِسْمِ الثَّالِثِ فَيَبْطُلُ قِيَاسُهُ عَلَى الْبَوْلِ؛ لِفَسَادِ الْوَصْفِ الْجَامِعِ.
translated_text:
The sixth argument:

It passes through the urinary passage and thus becomes impure through contact with urine, like milk in an impure vessel. All these proofs therefore establish its impurity.

We reply—and it is for Allah to show the right way:

As for the hadith of ʿAmmār ibn Yāsir, it has no basis. Its chain of transmission includes Thābit ibn Hammād, whom al-Dāraqutnī described as “very weak.” Ibn ʿAdī said: “He transmits objectionable reports.” The hadith of ʿĀʾishah has already been discussed.

As for the second argument, they say that it necessitates purification from both physical and ritual impurity. We do not concede that it necessitates purification from physical impurity. Rather, washing the private parts after its discharge is recommended, just as removing it from clothing and the body is recommended. Some have held that this washing is obligatory, just as some have held that washing the testicles after the discharge of pre-ejaculatory fluid is obligatory, and just as washing the limbs of ablution becomes obligatory when something leaves the private parts. These are all instances of purification required because of a discharge, even though their purpose need not be to remove it or to deem it impure. Rather, they are required for another reason, just as the rest of the body is washed because of it. In short, the reason for washing the private parts after its discharge is not impurity, but something else.

Thus, their statement that it “necessitates purification from physical impurity” asserts a characteristic that is not conceded in the case being compared. Washing it from the private parts is not done because of physical impurity, nor are acts of purification confined to removing such impurity. Examples include washing the hands upon rising from a night’s sleep, washing the deceased, recommended ritual baths, washing the testicles, and other such acts.

Accordingly, if this purification is held to be obligatory, it belongs to the third category. The analogy between semen and urine therefore fails, because the alleged common characteristic is invalid.

 وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُمْ:
 التَّطْهِيرُ مِنْهُ أَبْعَدُ مِنْ تَطْهِيرِهِ. فَجَمَعَ مَا بَيْنَ مُتَفَاوِتَيْنِ
translated_text:
As for its necessitating purification from ritual impurity, that is true. However, the causes requiring such purification are not confined to impure substances. Minor ritual purification is required after passing wind, by consensus. The evidence also establishes that it is required after touching with desire, touching the private parts, eating camel meat, apostasy, and washing the deceased. In the early days of Islam, it was also required after eating anything cooked over fire. None of these causes is itself impure.

As for major ritual purification, it is required after penetration, when the two circumcised parts meet, even without any impurity. It is also required, according to a preferred view, after childbirth unaccompanied by bleeding, although the child is pure. It is required upon death, although the deceased is not deemed impure. According to some scholars, it is also required upon embracing Islam.

Their statement, “Whatever necessitates purification from ritual impurity, or requires a ritual bath, is impure,” is therefore contradicted by these numerous cases and does not hold universally. If they add to the effective cause the condition that it be something discharged from the body, wind and a newborn child provide decisive counterexamples.

Furthermore, it may be said: Your qualification “discharged” is merely an incidental attribute and cannot therefore be used to exclude counterexamples.

The converse is also false, and the attribute has no bearing on the ruling. Many things that do not necessitate purification from ritual impurity are nevertheless impure, such as blood that has not flowed and a small amount of vomit. Moreover, the distinction will be explained later, if Allah Most High wills. These, then, are three or four grounds of rebuttal.

As for their statement, “The purification required because of it is more far-reaching than cleansing the substance itself,” this conflates two unequal things

 وَهُوَ إلْحَاقُهُ بِالْمَذْيِ فَقَدْ مُنِعَ الْحُكْمُ فِي الْأَصْلِ عَلَى قَوْلٍ بِطَهَارَةِ الْمَذْيِ وَالْأَكْثَرُونَ سَلَّمُوهُ وَفَرَّقُوا بِافْتِرَاقِ الْحَقِيقَتَيْنِ؛ فَإِنَّ هَذَا يُخْلَقُ مِنْهُ الْوَلَدُ الَّذِي هُوَ أَصْلُ الْإِنْسَانِ وَذَلِكَ بِخِلَافِهِ. أَلَا
translated_text:
and distinct in nature. For purification necessitated by it removes ritual impurity, whereas cleansing the substance itself removes physical impurity. These are two categories that differ in their essential nature, causes, and rulings in many respects.

The former requires an intention, whereas the latter does not. The former involves performing what is commanded; the latter involves avoiding what is prohibited. The former is restricted to water or earth, whereas the latter may be accomplished without water in certain circumstances by agreement, and in others according to one scholarly view. The ruling of the former extends beyond the site of its cause to the entire body, whereas that of the latter is confined to its location. The former is required on parts other than the site of its cause, or on both that site and other parts; the latter is required only at the site of its cause. The former is apprehended through the senses, whereas the latter is apprehended through reason. The former generally follows the patterns of analogical reasoning employed by investigators, whereas the latter resists examination by analogy. The former is obligatory by agreement, whereas the obligation of the other is subject to a well-known disagreement. The former has a substitute, whereas there is a clear disagreement concerning a substitute for the latter specifically when it concerns the body.

In short, drawing an analogy between these two forms of purification is like drawing an analogy between prayer and Hajj merely because both are acts of worship, despite their different essential natures.

As for the third argument—drawing an analogy between semen and pre-ejaculatory fluid—the ruling concerning the original case has been disputed on the view that pre-ejaculatory fluid is pure. Most scholars, however, accept that ruling but distinguish between the two because their natures differ: the child, the beginning of a human being, is created from the former, but not the latter. see that failure to ejaculate is a defect upon which many rulings are based, all stemming from its being a deficiency? Frequent emissions of pre-ejaculatory fluid, however, may constitute an illness. It is mere waste, without any benefit, like urine. Although both are emitted as a result of sexual desire, semen is not pure merely because it results from sexual desire; there is another reason. If we treat it in the same way, we shall discuss that, if Allah Most High wills.

As for its being a derivative, that is not so. Rather, it is comparable to an incompletely formed fetus: when a woman miscarries a human fetus before its formation is complete, although it represents the beginning of human creation, very few of the rulings concerning human beings apply to it. Even if it were a derivative, impurity consists in being regarded as foul, and regarding a derivative as foul does not entail that its source is foul—as with the waste products discharged by a human being.

As for the fourth argument, drawing an analogy between semen and all other discharges on the grounds that they share the same outlet is refuted by the mouth: it is the outlet for phlegm and saliva, both of which are pure, as well as vomit, which is impure. Likewise, the anus is the outlet for wind, which is pure, and feces, which are impure. The nose, too, is the outlet for mucus, which is pure, and blood, which is impure.

We also ask: Why do you say that the determining factor is the outlet? Why should it not instead be the origin and transformation of the substance? Whatever is formed in the upper body would then be pure, and whatever is formed in the lower body impure. Semen emerges from between the backbone and the ribs, unlike urine and post-urinary discharge. This criterion is more consistent: vomit and phlegm deemed impure both emerge from the mouth, yet they are impure because they have undergone transformation in the stomach. We shall also explain the distinction, if Allah Most High wills.

Second, a defining characteristic of impurity is that it must be avoided during prayer. This requirement does not apply to blood and other substances within the body. Do you not see that the prayer of someone carrying a sealed vessel containing blood is invalid? If you say, “It is excused because of the difficulty of avoiding it,” I reply, “Rather, it is deemed pure because of the difficulty of avoiding it.” What precludes this, when the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, explains the purity of cats by the difficulty of avoiding them, saying:

“It is not impure; it is among those, male and female, who move about among you”?

Indeed, I would go further: we have seen that difficulty in avoidance is a consideration that warrants concessions. If avoiding an entire category is difficult, the whole category is exempted and consequently deemed pure. If the difficulty concerns only part of it, only the amount that is difficult to avoid is exempted. Here, it is difficult to avoid everything inside bodies, so this entire class is deemed pure, just as cats and smaller creatures are. This constitutes a third argument.

The fifth argument:

The presumption is purity; impurity can therefore be established only by evidence. None of the evidence or defining characteristics of impurity applies to this blood regarded as foul.

The sixth argument:

We have observed that the status of substances differs according to whether they remain where they perform their function and provide their benefit or have left that place. Water used for purification remains pure and purifying as long as it flows over the body parts of the person purifying himself; once it separates, its status changes. Likewise, while water remains on an impure surface, it continues to perform its cleansing function. This can only be because it is itself pure and purifying. Once it leaves the place where it performs its function, however, it is either impure or no longer purifying.

This is so even though water used in purification is sometimes altered by pure substances and sometimes by impurities. If admixture—the strongest cause of alteration—has no effect while the water is serving our purposes and benefiting us, what, then, of a substance in its own place of function, as created and governed by Allah? Understand this well, for it is the very essence of jurisprudence.

The third response to the underlying argument:

Even if we concede that blood is impure, it has undergone transformation and changed into something else.

As for their assertion, “Transformation does not render a substance pure,” we reply: Who issued such a sweeping fatwa, contrary to consensus?

 الِاسْتِقْرَاءُ دَلَّنَا أَنَّ كُلَّ مَا بَدَأَ اللَّهُ بِتَحْوِيلِهِ وَتَبْدِيلِهِ مِنْ جِنْسٍ إلَى جِنْسٍ مِثْلُ جَعْلِ الْخَمْرِ خَلًّا وَالدَّمِ مَنِيًّا وَالْعَلَقَةِ مُضْغَةً وَلَحْمِ الْجَلَّالَةِ الْخَبِيثِ طَيِّبًا وَكَذَلِكَ بَيْضُهَا وَلَبَنُهَا وَالزَّرْعُ الْمَسْقِيُّ بِالنَّجِسِ إذَا سُقِيَ بِالْمَاءِ الطَّاهِرِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّهُ يَزُولُ حُكْمُ التَّنْجِيسِ وَيَزُولُ حَقِيقَةُ النَّجِسِ وَاسْمُهُ التَّابِعُ لِلْحَقِيقَةِ وَهَذَا ضَرُورِيٌّ لَا يُمْكِنُ الْمُنَازَعَةُ فِيهِ؛ فَإِنَّ جَمِيعَ الْأَجْسَامِ الْمَخْلُوقَةِ فِي الْأَرْضِ فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ يُحَوِّلُهَا مِنْ حَالٍ إلَى حَالٍ وَيُبَدِّلُهَا خَلْقًا بَعْدَ خَلْقٍ وَلَا الْتِفَاتَ إلَى مَوَادِّهَا وَعَنَاصِرِهَا. وَأَمَّا مَا اسْتَحَالَ بِسَبَبِ كَسْبِ الْإِنْسَانِ كَإِحْرَاقِ الرَّوْثِ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ رَمَادًا وَوَضْعِ الْخِنْزِيرِ فِي الْمَلَّاحَةِ حَتَّى يَصِيرَ مِلْحًا فَفِيهِ خِلَافٌ مَشْهُورٌ. وَلِلْقَوْلِ بِالتَّطْهِيرِ اتِّجَاهٌ وَظُهُورُ وَمَسْأَلَتِنَا مِنْ الْقِسْمِ الْأَوَّلِ وَلِلَّهِ الْحَمْدُ.
 الدَّلِيلُ الْخَامِسُ:
 أَنَّ الْمَنِيَّ مُخَالِفٌ لِجَمِيعِ مَا يَخْرُجُ مِنْ الذَّكَرِ فِي خَلْقِهِ فَإِنَّهُ غَلِيظٌ وَتِلْكَ رَقِيقَةٌ. وَفِي لَوْنِهِ فَإِنَّهُ أَبْيَضُ شَدِيدُ الْبَيَاضِ. وَفِي رِيحِهِ فَإِنَّهُ طَيِّبٌ كَرَائِحَةِ الطَّلْعِ وَتِلْكَ خَبِيثَةٌ.
 ثُمَّ جَعَلَهُ اللَّهُ أَصْلًا لِجَمِيعِ أَنْبِيَائِهِ وَأَوْلِيَائِهِ وَعِبَادِهِ الصَّالِحِينَ وَالْإِنْسَانِ الْمُكَرَّمِ فَكَيْفَ يَكُونُ أَصْلُهُ نَجِسًا وَلِهَذَا قَالَ ابْنُ عَقِيلٍ:
 وَقَدْ نَاظَرَ بَعْضَ مَنْ يَقُولُ بِنَجَاسَتِهِ
translated_text:
For the Muslims unanimously agree that when Allah begins to break wine down and turn it into vinegar, it becomes pure. The same applies to transformations involving animals and trees. Indeed, I would go further:

An examination of the various cases shows us that whenever Allah begins to transform and change something from one kind into another—as when He turns wine into vinegar, blood into semen, a clinging clot into a lump of flesh, or the foul flesh of animals that feed on filth into wholesome flesh—the ruling of impurity ceases to apply. The same holds for their eggs and milk, and for crops irrigated with impure water when they are subsequently irrigated with pure water, and other such cases. The impure substance no longer exists as such, nor does the designation corresponding to its nature. This is self-evident and cannot be disputed. Allah transforms all created bodies on earth from one state into another, giving them one form after another, without regard to their original materials and constituent elements.

As for transformation brought about by human action, such as burning dung until it becomes ash or placing a pig in a salt bed until it becomes salt, there is a well-known disagreement concerning it. The view that such transformation renders a substance pure has clear and reasonable grounds. Our present question, however, belongs to the first category, and all praise belongs to Allah.

The fifth argument:

Semen differs from everything else discharged from the penis in its consistency: it is thick, whereas those other fluids are thin. It also differs in colour, being intensely white, and in smell, being pleasant like the scent of date-palm blossoms, whereas the others smell foul.

Moreover, Allah made it the origin of all His prophets, His allies, His righteous servants, and the human being whom He has honoured. How, then, could the human being’s origin be impure? This is why Ibn ‘Aqīl—who had debated someone who maintained that it was impure—said

لِرَجُلِ قَالَ لَهُ:
 مَا بَالُك وَبَالُ هَذَا؟
 قَالَ:
 أُرِيدَ أَنْ أَجْعَلَ أَصْلَهُ طَاهِرًا وَهُوَ يَأْبَى إلَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ نَجِسًا ثُمَّ لَيْسَ شَأْنُهُ شَأْنَ الْفُضُولِ بَلْ شَأْنَ مَا هُوَ غِذَاءٌ وَمَادَّةٌ فِي الْأَبْدَانِ إذْ هُوَ قِوَامُ النَّسْلِ فَهُوَ بِالْأُصُولِ أَشْبَهُ مِنْهُ بِالْفَضْلِ.
 الدَّلِيلُ السَّادِسُ:
 وَفِيهِ أَجْوِبَةٌ: (أَحَدُهَا لَا نُسَلِّمُ أَنَّهُ يَجْرِي فِي مَجْرَى الْبَوْلِ فَقَدْ قِيلَ: إنَّ بَيْنَهُمَا جِلْدَةٌ رَقِيقَةٌ وَإِنَّ الْبَوْلَ إنَّمَا يَخْرُجُ رَشْحًا وَهَذَا مَشْهُورٌ. وَبِالْجُمْلَةِ فَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ بَيَانِ اتِّصَالِهِمَا وَلَيْسَ ذَلِكَ مَعْلُومًا إلَّا فِي ثُقْبِ الذَّكَرِ وَهُوَ طَاهِرٌ أَوْ مَعْفُوٌّ عَنْ نَجَاسَتِهِ.
 الْوَجْهُ الثَّانِي:
 أَنَّهُ لَوْ جَرَى فِي مَجْرَاهُ فَلَا نُسَلِّمُ أَنَّ الْبَوْلَ قَبْلَ ظُهُورِهِ نَجِسٌ. كَمَا مَرَّ تَقْرِيرُهُ فِي الدَّمِ وَهُوَ فِي الدَّمِ أَبْيَنُ مِنْهُ فِي الْبَوْلِ؛ لِأَنَّ ذَلِكَ رُكْنٌ وَبَعْضُ وَهَذَا فَضْلٌ.
 الْوَجْهُ الثَّالِثُ:
 أَنَّهُ لَوْ كَانَ نَجِسًا فَلَا نُسَلِّمُ أَنَّ الْمُمَاسَّةَ فِي بَاطِنِ الْحَيَوَانِ مُوجِبَةٌ لِلتَّنْجِيسِ. كَمَا قَدْ قِيلَ فِي الِاسْتِحَالَةِ وَهُوَ فِي الْمُمَاسَّةِ أَبْيَنُ. يُؤَيِّدُ هَذَا قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{مِنْ بَيْنِ فَرْثٍ وَدَمٍ لَبَنًا خَالِصًا سَائِغًا لِلشَّارِبِينَ}
 وَلَوْ كَانَتْ الْمُمَاسَّةُ فِي الْبَاطِنِ لِلْفَرْثِ مَثَلًا مُوجِبَةً لِلنَّجَاسَةِ لَنُجِّسَ اللَّبَنُ.
translated_text:
to a man who asked him, “What is this dispute between you two about?” He replied, “I want to establish that his origin is pure, but he insists that it is impure.”

Moreover, semen is not like bodily waste; rather, it resembles the substances that nourish and constitute the body, since it is the basis of procreation. It thus has more in common with essential bodily constituents than with waste.

The sixth argument:

There are several responses to it.

First, we do not concede that semen passes through the urinary passage. It has been said that a thin membrane separates the two passages and that urine emerges only by seepage. This is a well-known view. In any event, it must be demonstrated that the two passages connect. This is known only at the opening of the penis, which is pure, or whose impurity is excused.

The second response:

Even if semen passes through the urinary passage, we do not concede that urine is impure before it emerges, as previously explained regarding blood. This is clearer in the case of blood than of urine, since blood is an essential constituent and part of the body, whereas urine is waste.

The third response:

Even if urine is impure, we do not concede that contact inside a living creature renders something impure. The same point has already been made concerning transformation, and it is clearer still in the case of mere contact. This is supported by the words of Allah, Exalted is He:

“From between digested matter and blood, pure milk, pleasant for those who drink it.”

If internal contact with digested matter, for example, caused impurity, the milk would become impure.

فَإِنْ قِيلَ:
 فَلَعَلَّ بَيْنَهُمَا حَاجِزًا.
 قِيلَ:
 الْأَصْلُ عَدَمُهُ عَلَى أَنَّ ذِكْرَهُ هَذَا فِي مَعْرِضِ بَيَانِ ذِكْرِ الِاقْتِدَارِ بِإِخْرَاجِ طَيِّبٍ مِنْ بَيْنِ خَبِيثَيْنِ فِي الِاغْتِذَاءِ وَلَا يَتِمُّ إلَّا مَعَ عَدَمِ الْحَاجِزِ وَإِلَّا فَهُوَ مَعَ الْحَاجِزِ ظَاهِرٌ فِي كَمَالِ خَلْقِهِ سُبْحَانَهُ.
 وَكَذَلِكَ قَوْلُهُ:
 
{خَالِصًا}
 وَالْخُلُوصُ لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ مَعَ قِيَامِ الْمُوجِبِ لِلشُّرْبِ وَبِالْجُمْلَةِ فَخُرُوجُ اللَّبَنِ مِنْ بَيْنِ الْفَرْثِ وَالدَّمِ أَشْبَهُ شَيْءٍ بِخُرُوجِ الْمَنِيِّ مِنْ مَخْرَجِ الْبَوْلِ وَقَدْ سَلَكَ هَذَا الْمَسْلَكَ مَنْ رَأَى إنْفَحَةَ الْمَيْتَةِ وَلَبَنَهَا طَاهِرًا لِأَنَّهُ كَانَ طَاهِرًا وَإِنَّمَا حَدَثُ نَجَاسَةِ الْوِعَاءِ فَقَالَ: الْمُلَاقَاةُ فِي الْبَاطِنِ غَيْرُ ظَاهِرٍ. وَمَنْ نَجَّسَ هَذَا فَرَّقَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ الْمَنِيِّ بِأَنَّ الْمَنِيَّ يَنْفَصِلُ عَنْ النَّجِسِ فِي الْبَاطِنِ أَيْضًا بِخِلَافِ اللَّبَنِ فَإِنَّهُ لَا يُمْكِنُ فَصْلُهُ مِنْ الْمَيْتَةِ إلَّا بَعْدَ إبْرَازِ الضَّرْعِ وَحِينَئِذٍ يَصِيرُ فِي حَدِّ مَا يَلْحَقُهُ النَّجَاسَةُ. 
{وَاللَّهُ يَقُولُ الْحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهْدِي السَّبِيلَ}
 وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَسَلَامٌ عَلَى عِبَادِهِ الَّذِينَ اصْطَفَى. وَهَذَا الَّذِي حَضَرَنِي فِي هَذَا الْوَقْتِ وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إلَّا بِاَللَّهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ.
translated_text:
If it is said, “Perhaps there is a barrier between them,” the reply is:

The presumption is that there is none. Moreover, this is mentioned to demonstrate His power to bring forth something wholesome for consumption from between two unwholesome substances. This demonstration is complete only if there is no barrier. With a barrier in place, however, the outcome would be evident from the perfection of His creation—glory be to Him.

The same applies to His words, “pure.” Such purity must coexist with that which gives cause to drink. In short, milk emerging from between digested matter and blood closely resembles semen emerging through the urinary passage.

Those who consider the rennet and milk of an animal that died without lawful slaughter to be pure have followed this line of reasoning: the contents were pure, and impurity arose only in their container. They therefore say, “Internal contact is not outward contact.” Those who regard these as impure distinguish them from semen on the grounds that semen also separates from the impure substance internally. Milk, by contrast, cannot be separated from the dead animal until the udder is exposed; at that point, it comes within the category of things susceptible to impurity.

“Allah speaks the truth, and He guides to the right way.”

Praise be to Allah, and peace be upon His servants whom He has chosen. This is what has occurred to me at this time. There is neither power nor strength except through Allah, the Most High, the Magnificent.

وَسُئِلَ:
 
(*)
عَنْ الْمَنِيِّ هَلْ هُوَ طَاهِرٌ أَمْ لَا؟ وَإِذَا كَانَ طَاهِرًا فَمَا حُكْمُ رُطُوبَةِ فَرْجِ الْمَرْأَةِ إذَا خَالَطَهُ؟.
فَأَجَابَ:
وَأَمَّا الْمَنِيُّ فَالصَّحِيحُ أَنَّهُ طَاهِرٌ كَمَا هُوَ مَذْهَبُ الشَّافِعِيِّ وَأَحْمَد فِي الْمَشْهُورِ عَنْهُ.
 وَقَدْ قِيلَ:
 إنَّهُ نَجِسٌ يُجْزِئُ فَرْكُهُ؛ كَقَوْلِ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَأَحْمَد فِي رِوَايَةٍ أُخْرَى وَهَلْ يُعْفَى عَنْ يَسِيرِهِ كَالدَّمِ أَوْ لَا يُعْفَى عَنْهُ كَالْبَوْلِ؟ عَلَى قَوْلَيْنِ هُمَا رِوَايَتَانِ عَنْ أَحْمَد.
 وَقِيلَ:
 إنَّهُ يَجِبُ غَسْلُهُ كَقَوْلِ مَالِكٍ وَالْأَوَّلُ هُوَ الصَّوَابُ فَإِنَّهُ مِنْ الْمَعْلُومِ أَنَّ الصَّحَابَةَ كَانُوا يَحْتَلِمُونَ عَلَى عَهْدِ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ وَأَنَّ الْمَنِيَّ يُصِيبُ بَدَنَ أَحَدِهِمْ وَثِيَابَهُ وَهَذَا مِمَّا تَعُمُّ بِهِ الْبَلْوَى فَلَوْ كَانَ ذَلِكَ نَجِسًا لَكَانَ يَجِبُ عَلَى النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَمْرُهُمْ بِإِزَالَةِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أَبْدَانِهِمْ وَثِيَابِهِمْ كَمَا أَمَرَهُمْ بِالِاسْتِنْجَاءِ وَكَمَا أَمَرَ الْحَائِضَ بِأَنْ تَغْسِلَ دَمَ الْحَيْضِ مِنْ ثَوْبِهَا بَلْ إصَابَةُ النَّاسِ الْمَنِيَّ أَعْظَمُ بِكَثِيرِ مِنْ

translated_text:
He was also asked: (*)

Is semen pure or not? If it is pure, what is the ruling on a woman’s vaginal moisture when it mixes with it?

He replied:

As for semen, the correct view is that it is pure. This is the position of al-Shāfi‘ī and the well-known view reported from Ahmad.

It has also been said that it is impure, but rubbing it off suffices. This is the position of Abū Hanīfa and another view reported from Ahmad. Is a small amount of it excused, as with blood, or not excused, as with urine? There are two views, both reported from Ahmad.

It has also been said that it must be washed off, as Mālik held. The first view, however, is correct. It is well known that the Companions experienced nocturnal emissions during the Prophet’s lifetime, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and that semen would get onto their bodies and clothes. This was a widespread occurrence. Had it been impure, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would have been obliged to instruct them to remove it from their bodies and clothes, just as he instructed them to cleanse themselves after relieving themselves and instructed menstruating women to wash menstrual blood from their clothes. Shaykh Nāsir ibn Hamad al-Fahd stated (p. 176):
There are two points here:
First: This same fatwa is repeated immediately after this passage in the same volume, 21:606–607, but with thirteen lines omitted: from “It has been said that it is impure” (the sixth line of 21:604) to “This is conclusive for anyone who reflects on it” (the fourth line of 21:605).
Second: At 21:606, the wording is: “And where avoidance is difficult—and semen is difficult to avoid—it was accorded the same ruling as the outlet.” At 21:607, however, it reads: “And where avoidance is difficult, it was accorded the same ruling as the outlet.” Thus, the phrase “and semen is difficult to avoid” was omitted because the copyist’s eye skipped between the repeated phrases. He—may Allah have mercy on him—was also asked:

“What is the ruling on pottery fired using impure substances, and on ovens heated with dung?”

He answered:

Praise be to Allah.

These questions rest on two principles. The first concerns using impure dung and similar substances as fuel to heat water or food and the like.

Some jurists among the followers of Ahmad and others said that this is impermissible because it involves handling and coming into direct contact with impurity. Others said that it is disliked but not forbidden, because destroying impure substances is not forbidden; rather, such use poses a risk of becoming soiled with them.

A similar case is using impure oil for lighting, since this is a use that consumes it. The well-known position reported from Ahmad and other scholars is that this is permissible, and this is what is transmitted from the Companions. The other position reported from him and others is that it is prohibited, because it poses a risk of becoming soiled with it, and because smoke from impure substances is disliked.

The correct view is that none of this is forbidden. For Allah Most High has forbidden foul things, such as blood, carrion and swine flesh, and it is authentically reported in the two Sahīh collections from the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—

 فَإِنَّ الرُّخْصَةَ الْمُتَقَدِّمَةَ كَانَتْ فِي الِانْتِفَاعِ بِالْجُلُودِ بِلَا دِبَاغٍ كَمَا ذَهَبَ إلَيْهِ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ السَّلَفِ فَرَفَعَ النَّهْيَ عَمَّا أَرْخَصَ فَأَمَّا الِانْتِفَاعُ بِهَا بَعْدَ الدِّبَاغِ فَلَمْ يَنْهَ عَنْهُ قَطُّ وَلِهَذَا كَانَ آخِرُ الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَد: أَنَّ الدِّبَاغَ مُطَهِّرٌ لِجُلُودِ الْمَيْتَةِ: لَكِنْ هَلْ يَقُومُ مَقَامَ الذَّكَاةِ أَوْ مَقَامَ الْحَيَاةِ فَيُطَهِّرُ جِلْدَ الْمَأْكُولِ أَوْ جِلْدَ مَا كَانَ طَاهِرًا فِي الْحَيَاةِ دُونَ مَا سِوَى ذَلِكَ؟
 عَلَى وَجْهَيْنِ:
 أَصَحُّهُمَا الْأَوَّلُ. فَيَطْهُرُ بِالدِّبَاغِ مَا تُطَهِّرُهُ الذَّكَاةُ لِنَهْيِهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فِي حَدِيثٍ عَنْ جُلُودِ السِّبَاعِ. وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّ اسْتِعْمَالَ الْخَمْرِ فِي إطْفَاءِ الْحَرِيقِ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ سَلَّمَهُ الْمُنَازِعُونَ مَعَ أَنَّ الْأَمْرَ بِمُجَانَبَةِ الْخَمْرِ أَعْظَمُ فَإِذَا جَازَ إتْلَافُ الْخَمْرِ بِمَا فِيهِ مَنْفَعَةٌ فَإِتْلَافُ النَّجَاسَاتِ بِمَا لَيْسَ فِيهِ مَنْفَعَةٌ أَوْلَى؛ وَلِأَنَّهُمْ سَلَّمُوا جَوَازَ طَعَامِ الْمَيْتَةِ لِلْبُزَاةِ وَالصُّقُورِ فَاسْتِعْمَالُهَا فِي النَّارِ أَوْلَى.
 وَأَمَّا قَوْلُ الْقَائِلِ:
 هَذَا مَظِنَّةُ مُلَابَسَتِهَا فَيُقَالُ: مُلَابَسَةُ النَّجَاسَةِ لِلْحَاجَةِ جَائِزٌ إذَا طَهَّرَ بَدَنَهُ وَثِيَابَهُ عِنْدَ الصَّلَاةِ وَنَحْوِهَا. كَمَا يَجُوزُ الِاسْتِنْجَاءُ بِالْمَاءِ مَعَ مُبَاشَرَةِ النَّجَاسَةِ وَلَا يُكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ عَلَى أَصَحِّ الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَد وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَكْثَرِ الْفُقَهَاءِ.
 وَالرِّوَايَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ:
 يُكْرَهُ ذَلِكَ.
translated_text:
that he said:

“Only eating carrion has been forbidden.”

He subsequently prohibited wearing its hide before tanning. This explains his words in the hadith of ‘Abd Allāh ibn ‘Ukaym:

“I had permitted you to use the hides of dead animals. But when this letter of mine reaches you, do not make use of their hides or sinews.”

The earlier concession concerned using hides without tanning, as a group of the early generations held. The prohibition thus revoked the earlier concession. As for using them after tanning, he never prohibited that. Accordingly, the later of the two positions reported from Ahmad was that tanning purifies the hides of dead animals. But does tanning take the place of ritual slaughter, purifying the hides of animals lawful to eat, or the place of life, purifying the hides of animals that were pure while alive, but not others? There are two views. The sounder is the first: tanning purifies whatever ritual slaughter purifies, because the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—forbade the use of the hides of predatory animals in a hadith.

Moreover, those who disagree concede that wine may be used to extinguish fires and for similar purposes, even though the command to avoid wine is more emphatic. If wine may be destroyed in a way that yields benefit, then destroying impure substances in a way that yields no benefit is all the more permissible. They also concede that carrion may be fed to hawks and falcons, so using it as fuel is all the more permissible.

As for the objection, “This poses a risk of coming into contact with impurity,” the answer is that contact with impurity when needed is permissible, provided one purifies one’s body and clothing for prayer and similar acts. Thus, it is permissible to cleanse oneself with water after relieving oneself, despite direct contact with impurity. This is not disliked according to the sounder of the two positions reported from Ahmad, and this is the view of most jurists. The second position is that it is disliked.

original_text:
بَلْ يُسْتَعْمَلُ الْحَجَرُ أَوْ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَهُمَا. وَالْمَشْهُورُ أَنَّ الِاقْتِصَارَ عَلَى الْمَاءِ أَفْضَلُ وَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهِ مُبَاشَرَتُهَا.
 وَفِي اسْتِعْمَالِ جُلُودِ الْمَيْتَةِ إذَا لَمْ يَقُلْ بِطَهَارَتِهَا فِي الْيَابِسَاتِ رِوَايَتَانِ:
 أَصَحُّهُمَا جَوَازُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنْ قِيلَ إنَّهُ يُكْرَهُ فَالْكَرَاهَةُ تَزُولُ بِالْحَاجَةِ.
 وَأَمَّا قَوْلُهُ:
 هَذَا يُفْضِي إلَى التَّلَوُّثِ بِدُخَّانِ النَّجَاسَةِ فَهَذَا مَبْنِيٌّ عَلَى الْأَصْلِ الثَّانِي وَهُوَ أَنَّ النَّجَاسَةَ فِي الْمَلَّاحَةِ إذَا صَارَتْ مِلْحًا وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ فَهَلْ هِيَ نَجِسَةٌ أَمْ لَا؟ عَلَى قَوْلَيْنِ مَشْهُورَيْنِ لِلْعُلَمَاءِ هُمَا رِوَايَتَانِ عَنْ أَحْمَد نَصَّ عَلَيْهِمَا فِي الْخِنْزِيرِ الْمَشْوِيِّ فِي التَّنُّورِ هَلْ تُطَهِّرُ النَّارُ مَا لَصِقَ بِهِ أَمْ يَحْتَاجُ إلَى غَسْلِ مَا أَصَابَهُ مِنْهُ؟
 عَلَى رِوَايَتَيْنِ مَنْصُوصَتَيْنِ:
أَحَدُهُمَا هِيَ نَجِسَةٌ وَهَذَا مَذْهَبُ الشَّافِعِيِّ. وَأَكْثَرِ أَصْحَابِ أَحْمَد وَأَحَدُ قَوْلَيْ أَصْحَابِ مَالِكٍ.
 وَهَؤُلَاءِ يَقُولُونَ:
 لَا يَطْهُرُ مِنْ النَّجَاسَةِ بِالِاسْتِحَالَةِ إلَّا الْخَمْرَةُ الْمُنْتَقِلَةُ بِنَفْسِهَا وَالْجِلْدُ الْمَدْبُوغُ إذَا قِيلَ إنَّ الدَّبْغَ إحَالَةٌ لَا إزَالَةٌ. وَالْقَوْلُ الثَّانِي وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَأَحَدُ قَوْلَيْ الْمَالِكِيَّةِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ أَنَّهَا لَا تَبْقَى نَجِسَةً. وَهَذَا هُوَ الصَّوَابُ فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ الْأَعْيَانَ لَمْ يَتَنَاوَلْهَا نَصُّ التَّحْرِيمِ لَا لَفْظًا وَلَا مَعْنًى وَلَيْسَتْ فِي مَعْنَى النُّصُوصِ
translated_text:
Rather, stones should be used, or both methods combined. The well-known view, however, is that using water alone is preferable, even though it involves direct contact with impurity.

Regarding the use of carrion hides for dry substances, on the view that these hides are not pure, there are two positions reported from Ahmad. The sounder permits this; even if it is considered disliked, that disapproval is lifted when there is a need.

As for the objection, “This leads to contamination with smoke from impure substances,” this rests on the second principle: if an impure substance in a salt bed turns into salt, or undergoes a similar transformation, does it remain impure? Scholars hold two well-known views, both reported from Ahmad. He explicitly stated both positions regarding a pig roasted in an oven: does fire purify the matter adhering to the oven, or must the parts soiled by the pig be washed?

There are two explicitly recorded positions. The first is that the substance remains impure. This is the position of al-Shāfi‘ī and most of Ahmad’s followers, and one of the two views held by Mālik’s followers. Those who hold this view say that no impure substance is purified through transformation except wine that transforms of its own accord, and tanned hide—if tanning is understood as transforming the impurity rather than removing it.

The second view, which is the position of Abū Hanīfah and one of the two views held by the Mālikīs and others, is that it no longer remains impure. This is the correct view, for these substances are not covered by the scriptural prohibition, either in wording or meaning, nor are they analogous to what those texts prohibit

original_text:
بَلْ هِيَ أَعْيَانٌ طَيِّبَةٌ فَيَتَنَاوَلُهَا نَصُّ التَّحْلِيلِ وَهِيَ أَوْلَى بِذَلِكَ مِنْ الْخَمْرِ الْمُنْقَلِبَةِ بِنَفْسِهَا وَمَا ذَكَرُوهُ مِنْ الْفَرْقِ بِأَنَّ الْخَمْرَ نَجُسَتْ بِالِاسْتِحَالَةِ فَتَطْهُرُ بِالِاسْتِحَالَةِ بَاطِلٌ؛
 فَإِنَّ جَمِيعَ النَّجَاسَاتِ إنَّمَا نَجُسَتْ بِالِاسْتِحَالَةِ:
 كَالدَّمِ فَإِنَّهُ مُسْتَحِيلٌ عَنْ الْغِذَاءِ الطَّاهِرِ وَكَذَلِكَ الْبَوْلُ وَالْعَذِرَةُ حَتَّى الْحَيَوَانُ النَّجِسُ مُسْتَحِيلٌ عَنْ الْمَاءِ وَالتُّرَابِ وَنَحْوِهِمَا مِنْ الطَّاهِرَاتِ. وَلَا يَنْبَغِي أَنْ يُعَبَّرَ عَنْ ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ النَّجَاسَةَ طَهُرَتْ بِالِاسْتِحَالَةِ فَإِنَّ نَفْسَ النَّجِسِ لَمْ يَطْهُرْ لَكِنْ اسْتَحَالَ وَهَذَا الطَّاهِرُ لَيْسَ هُوَ ذَلِكَ النَّجِسَ وَإِنْ كَانَ مُسْتَحِيلًا مِنْهُ وَالْمَادَّةُ وَاحِدَةٌ كَمَا أَنَّ الْمَاءَ لَيْسَ هُوَ الزَّرْعَ وَالْهَوَاءَ وَالْحَبَّ وَتُرَابُ الْمَقْبَرَةِ لَيْسَ هُوَ الْمَيِّتَ وَالْإِنْسَانُ لَيْسَ هُوَ الْمَنِيَّ. وَاَللَّهُ تَعَالَى يَخْلُقُ أَجْسَامَ الْعَالَمِ بَعْضَهَا مِنْ بَعْضٍ وَيُحِيلُ بَعْضَهَا إلَى بَعْضٍ وَهِيَ تُبَدَّلُ مَعَ الْحَقَائِقِ لَيْسَ هَذَا هَذَا. فَكَيْفَ يَكُونُ الرَّمَادُ هُوَ الْعَظْمَ الْمَيِّتَ وَاللَّحْمَ وَالدَّمَ نَفْسَهُ. بِمَعْنَى أَنَّهُ يَتَنَاوَلُهُ اسْمُ الْعَظْمِ. وَأَمَّا كَوْنُهُ هُوَ هُوَ بِاعْتِبَارِ الْأَصْلِ وَالْمَادَّةِ فَهَذَا لَا يَضُرُّ فَإِنَّ التَّحْرِيمَ يَتْبَعُ الِاسْمَ وَالْمَعْنَى الَّذِي هُوَ الْخَبَثُ وَكِلَاهُمَا مُنْتَفٍ. وَعَلَى هَذَا فَدُخَانُ النَّارِ الْمُوقَدَةِ بِالنَّجَاسَةِ طَاهِرٌ وَبُخَارُ الْمَاءِ النَّجِسِ الَّذِي يَجْتَمِعُ فِي السَّقْفِ طَاهِرٌ وَأَمْثَالُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْمَسَائِلِ
translated_text:
but are instead wholesome substances, and thus fall under the scriptural texts permitting such things. They have an even stronger claim to this ruling than wine that transforms of its own accord. The distinction they propose—that wine became impure through transformation and therefore becomes pure through transformation—is invalid. For all impure substances became impure through transformation: blood, for example, is transformed from pure food, as are urine and excrement. Even an impure animal is transformed from water, earth, and other pure substances.

It is not appropriate to describe this by saying that an impure substance has become pure through transformation. The impure substance itself has not become pure; rather, it has transformed. This pure substance is not that impure substance, even though it has been transformed from it and the underlying material is the same. Likewise, water is not crops, air, or grain; the soil of a graveyard is not the deceased; and a human being is not semen. Allah Most High creates the bodies of the world from one another and transforms them into one another. They change along with their essential natures: one is not the other.

How, then, can ashes be the very same dead bone, flesh, and blood—in the sense that the term “bone” applies to them? As for their being the same in origin and underlying material, this does not affect the ruling. Prohibition depends on the name and the quality of foulness it denotes, and both are absent here.

Accordingly, smoke from a fire fuelled by impure substances is pure, and vapour from impure water that collects on the ceiling is pure. The same applies to similar cases.

original_text:
وَإِذَا كَانَ كَذَلِكَ فَهَذَا الْفَخَّارُ طَاهِرٌ إذْ لَيْسَ فِيهِ مِنْ النَّجَاسَةِ شَيْءٌ.
 وَإِنْ قِيلَ:
 إنَّهُ خَالَطَهُ مِنْ دُخَانِهَا خَرَجَ عَلَى الْقَوْلَيْنِ وَالصَّحِيحُ أَنَّهُ طَاهِرٌ. وَأَمَّا نَفْسُ اسْتِعْمَالِ النَّجَاسَةِ فَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ الْكَلَامُ فِيهِ وَالنِّزَاعُ فِي الْمَاءِ الْمُسَخَّنِ بِالنَّجَاسَةِ فَإِنَّهُ طَاهِرٌ؛
 لَكِنْ هَلْ يُكْرَهُ عَلَى قَوْلَيْنِ:
 هُمَا رِوَايَتَانِ عَنْ أَحْمَد.
 إحْدَاهُمَا:
 لَا يُكْرَهُ وَهُوَ قَوْلُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ. وَالثَّانِي يُكْرَهُ وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ مَالِكٍ.
 وَلِلْكَرَاهَةِ مَأْخَذَانِ:
 أَحَدُهُمَا: خَشْيَةُ أَنْ يَكُونَ قَدْ وَصَلَ إلَى الْمَاءِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ النَّجَاسَةِ فَيُكْرَهُ لِاحْتِمَالِ تَنَجُّسِهِ فَعَلَى هَذَا إذَا كَانَ بَيْنَ الْمَوْقِدِ وَبَيْنَ النَّارِ حَاجِزٌ حَصِينٌ لَمْ يُكْرَهْ وَهَذِهِ طَرِيقَةُ الشَّرِيفِ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ وَابْنِ عَقِيلٍ وَغَيْرِهِمَا.
 وَالثَّانِي:
 أَنَّ سَبَبَ الْكَرَاهَةِ كَوْنُ اسْتِعْمَالِ النَّجَاسَةِ مَكْرُوهًا وَأَنَّ السُّخُونَةَ حَصَلَتْ بِفِعْلِ مَكْرُوهٍ وَهَذِهِ طَرِيقَةُ الْقَاضِي أَبِي يَعْلَى وَمِثْلُ هَذَا
translated_text:
And if that is so, this pottery is pure, since it contains no impurity.

If it is argued that some smoke from the impure fuel has mingled with it, its ruling would fall under the two opinions; the correct view is that it is pure. As for the use of impure substances itself, this has already been discussed. Water heated with impure fuel is pure, but there are two opinions on whether its use is disliked, both transmitted from Ahmad. The first is that it is not disliked, which is also the position of Abū Hanīfah and al-Shāfi‘ī. The second is that it is disliked, which is the position of Mālik.

There are two grounds for considering it disliked:

The first is the fear that some impurity may have reached the water, making its use disliked because it may have become impure. On this basis, if there is a solid barrier between the stove and the fire, its use is not disliked. This is the approach of al-Sharīf Abū Ja‘far, Ibn ‘Aqīl, and others.

The second is that using impure substances is itself disliked, and the heat was produced through a disliked act. This is the approach of al-Qādī Abū Ya‘lā. A similar case is

original_text:
طَبْخُ الطَّعَامِ بِالْوَقُودِ النَّجِسِ فَإِنْ نَضِجَ الطَّعَامُ كَسُخُونَةِ الْمَاءِ وَالْكَرَاهَةِ فِي طَبْخِ الْفَخَّارِ بِالْوَقُودِ النَّجِسِ تُشْبِهُ تَسْخِينَ الْمَاءِ الَّذِي لَيْسَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ النَّارِ حَاجِزٌ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ بَوْلِ مَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ:
 هَلْ هُوَ نَجِسٌ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
أَمَّا بَوْلُ مَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ وَرَوْثُ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّ أَكْثَرَ السَّلَفِ عَلَى أَنَّ ذَلِكَ لَيْسَ بِنَجِسِ وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ مَالِكٍ وَأَحْمَد وَغَيْرِهِمَا وَيُقَالُ:

He was asked:

“Is the urine of animals whose meat is lawful to eat impure?”

He answered:

Most of the early Muslims held that the urine and dung of animals whose meat is lawful to eat are not impure. This is the position of Mālik, Ahmad, and others. It is said that none of the Companions held them to be impure. Rather, the view that they are impure arose later, with no precedent among the Companions.

We have discussed this question at length in a separate book, presenting more than ten proofs from the Sharia showing that these substances are not impure. Those who consider them impure have no evidence whatsoever from the Sharia for their impurity. The most they have relied upon is the Prophet’s saying, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“Guard yourselves against urine.”

They assumed that this applies universally in all cases, but that is not so. The definite article here refers to something already understood, and the urine understood here is human urine. The evidence for this is his saying:

“Guard yourselves against urine, for most of the punishment in the grave is because of it.”

Yet he did not instruct them to wash whatever touched their mouths and hands, or to wash the vessels containing the urine, despite their having only recently embraced Islam. Had livestock urine been like human urine, explaining this would have been obligatory, and it would not have been permissible to delay that explanation beyond the time it was needed. This is especially so because he mentioned the urine together with the milk, which is lawful and pure. Moreover, the Prophet’s prohibition of treatment with foul substances, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is established through numerous reports.

Furthermore, it is established in the Sahīh that

Since the Sunnah permits this, anyone who equates human urine with sheep urine is contradicting the Sunnah.

He was asked about a baker who heats his oven with dung and bakes bread.

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If the dung is pure, such as the dung of cattle, sheep, camels, or horses, it does not render the bread impure.

If it is impure, such as the dung of mules, donkeys, and other beasts, then according to some scholars, if the dung is dry, the oven has dried out after contact with it, and it does not render the bread impure. If some of it sticks to the bread, that portion is removed, and the remainder is not rendered impure. And Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He was asked:

Is the dog pure or impure? What are the scholars’ views concerning it?

He replied:

The scholars hold three well-known views concerning the dog:

The first is that it is entirely impure, even its hair. This is the view of al-Shāfiʿī and one of the two opinions reported from Ahmad.

The second is that it is pure, even its saliva. This is the well-known view reported from Mālik.

The third is that its saliva is impure, but its hair is pure. This is the well-known position of Abū Hanīfah. This reported position is supported by most of his followers, and it is also the other opinion reported from Ahmad. This is the strongest of the three views.

Thus, if moisture from its hair comes into contact with clothing or the body, it does not render either impure. If it laps from water, the water is to be poured away. If it laps from milk or something similar, some scholars, such as Mālik and others, hold that the food may be consumed. Others hold that it is to be poured away; this is the position of Abū Hanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad. If, however, the milk is present in a large quantity, the correct view is that it does not become impure.

Three opinions are reported from Ahmad concerning hair growing on an impure part of the body:

The first is that all such hair is pure, even the hair of dogs and pigs. This is the view preferred by Abū Bakr ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz.

The second is that all such hair is impure, as al-Shāfiʿī holds.

The third is that the hair of a dead animal is pure if the animal was pure while alive, such as a sheep or a mouse; but the hair of an animal that is impure while alive, such as a dog or a pig, is impure. According to most of Ahmad’s followers, this is the position he explicitly stated.

The strongest view is that all hair is pure—the hair of dogs, pigs, and other animals—unlike saliva. Accordingly, if a dog’s hair is wet and touches a person’s clothing, nothing is required of that person. This is the position of the majority of jurists, including Abū Hanīfah, Mālik, and Ahmad according to one of the two opinions reported from him. This is because material things are presumed pure: nothing may be declared impure or forbidden without evidence. As Allah Most High says:

“He has already explained to you what He has forbidden you, except that to which you are compelled by necessity.”

And Allah Most High says:

“Allah would never lead a people astray after guiding them until He makes clear to them what they must avoid.”

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in an authentic hadith:

“Among the Muslims whose offence against their fellow Muslims is greatest is someone who asks about something that was not forbidden, only for it to become forbidden because of his question.”

The Sunan collections contain a report from Salmān al-Fārisī attributed to the Prophet, though some transmit it as a statement of Salmān himself:

“What is lawful is what Allah has made lawful in His Book, and what is forbidden is what Allah has forbidden in His Book. Whatever He has remained silent about is among the things He has pardoned.”

That being so, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“To purify the vessel of any one of you when a dog laps from it, wash it seven times, the first time with earth.”

Another hadith says: “If a dog laps.” Thus, all the hadiths on this matter mention only lapping; they do not mention the rest of the dog’s body. Declaring those other parts impure therefore rests solely on analogy.

 إنَّ الزَّرْعَ طَاهِرٌ فَالشَّعْرُ أَوْلَى وَمَنْ قَالَ إنَّ الزَّرْعَ نَجِسٌ فَإِنَّ الْفَرْقَ بَيْنَهُمَا مَا ذُكِرَ فَإِنَّ الزَّرْعَ يَلْحَقُ بِالْجَلَّالَةِ الَّتِي تَأْكُلُ النَّجَاسَةَ وَهَذَا أَيْضًا حُجَّةٌ فِي الْمَسْأَلَةِ فَإِنَّ الْجَلَّالَةَ الَّتِي تَأْكُلُ النَّجَاسَةَ قَدْ نَهَى النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ عَنْ لَبَنِهَا فَإِذَا حُبِسَتْ حَتَّى تَطِيبَ كَانَتْ حَلَالًا بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ؛ لِأَنَّهَا قَبْلَ ذَلِكَ يَظْهَرُ أَثَرُ النَّجَاسَةِ فِي لَبَنِهَا وَبَيْضِهَا وَعَرَقِهَا فَيَظْهَرُ نَتْنُ النَّجَاسَةِ وَخُبْثُهَا فَإِذَا زَالَ ذَلِكَ عَادَتْ طَاهِرَةً فَإِنَّ الْحُكْمَ إذَا ثَبَتَ بِعِلَّةِ زَالَ بِزَوَالِهَا. وَالشَّعْرُ لَا يَظْهَرُ فِيهِ شَيْءٌ مِنْ آثَارِ النَّجَاسَةِ أَصْلًا فَلَمْ يَكُنْ لِتَنْجِيسِهِ مَعْنًى.
translated_text:
Thus, if it is argued that urine is more impure than saliva, that is a valid point. Hair, however, cannot be treated as analogous to saliva, because saliva is secreted from within the dog, whereas hair grows on its exterior. All jurists distinguish between the two. Most of them hold that the hair of a dead animal is pure, unlike its saliva.

Al-Shāfi‘ī and most jurists hold that crops growing in impure soil are pure. At most, then, a dog’s hair grows in an impure place, like crops growing in impure soil. If crops are pure, hair has an even stronger claim to purity: crops contain moisture and softness in which the effects of impurity become apparent, whereas the dryness and solidity of hair prevent such effects from appearing.

Thus, for those of Ahmad’s followers, such as Ibn ‘Aqīl and others, who hold that crops are pure, hair has an even stronger claim to purity. As for those who hold that crops are impure, the distinction between crops and hair is what has just been explained: crops are analogous to animals that feed on impurities.

This also provides an argument on the issue. The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, forbade the milk of animals that feed on impurities. Yet if such an animal is confined until it becomes wholesome, it becomes lawful by agreement of the Muslims. Before that, the effects of impurity appear in its milk, eggs, and sweat, manifesting the impurity’s foul smell and offensive character. Once those effects disappear, it becomes pure again, for when a ruling is established on the basis of an operative cause, it ceases to apply when that cause disappears. Hair, however, shows none of the effects of impurity whatsoever, so there is no basis for declaring it impure.

original_text:
وَهَذَا يَتَبَيَّنُ بِالْكَلَامِ فِي شُعُورِ الْمَيْتَةِ كَمَا سَنَذْكُرُهُ إنْ شَاءَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى.
 وَكُلُّ حَيَوَانٍ قِيلَ بِنَجَاسَتِهِ فَالْكَلَامُ فِي شَعْرِهِ وَرِيشِهِ كَالْكَلَامِ فِي شَعْرِ الْكَلْبِ فَإِذَا قِيلَ:
 بِنَجَاسَةِ كُلِّ ذِي نَابٍ مِنْ السِّبَاعِ وَكُلِّ ذِي مِخْلَبٍ مِنْ الطَّيْرِ إلَّا الْهِرَّةَ وَمَا دُونَهَا فِي الْخِلْقَةِ.
 كَمَا هُوَ مَذْهَبُ كَثِيرٍ مِنْ الْعُلَمَاءِ:
 عُلَمَاءِ أَهْلِ الْعِرَاقِ وَهُوَ أَشْهَرُ الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَد فَإِنَّ الْكَلَامَ فِي رِيشِ ذَلِكَ وَشَعْرِهِ فِيهِ هَذَا النِّزَاعُ: هَلْ هُوَ نَجِسٌ؟
 عَلَى رِوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَد:
 إحْدَاهُمَا: أَنَّهُ طَاهِرٌ وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ الْجُمْهُورِ كَأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ وَمَالِكٍ.
 وَالرِّوَايَةُ الثَّانِيَةُ:
 أَنَّهُ نَجِسٌ كَمَا هُوَ اخْتِيَارُ كَثِيرٍ مِنْ مُتَأَخِّرِي أَصْحَابِ أَحْمَد وَالْقَوْلُ بِطَهَارَةِ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الصَّوَابُ. كَمَا تَقَدَّمَ. وَأَيْضًا فَالنَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ رَخَّصَ فِي اقْتِنَاءِ كَلْبِ الصَّيْدِ وَالْمَاشِيَةِ وَالْحَرْثِ وَلَا بُدَّ لِمَنْ اقْتَنَاهُ أَنْ يُصِيبَهُ رُطُوبَةُ شُعُورِهِ كَمَا يُصِيبُهُ رُطُوبَةُ الْبَغْلِ وَالْحِمَارِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ فَالْقَوْلُ بِنَجَاسَةِ شُعُورِهَا
translated_text:
This will become clear when we discuss the hair of dead animals, Allah Most High willing.

For every animal held to be impure, the discussion of its hair and feathers is the same as that of a dog’s hair. If one holds that every fanged beast of prey and every bird with talons is impure, except cats and creatures smaller than them—as is the view of many Iraqi scholars and the better-known of the two positions reported from Ahmad—then their feathers and hair are subject to this same disagreement: are they impure?

Two positions are reported from Ahmad. According to the first, they are pure; this is the view of the majority, including Abū Hanīfah, al-Shāfi‘ī, and Mālik. According to the second, they are impure; this is the position preferred by many of Ahmad’s later followers. The view that they are pure is correct, as explained above.

Moreover, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, permitted keeping dogs for hunting, guarding livestock, and protecting crops. Anyone who keeps a dog will inevitably come into contact with moisture from its hair, just as one comes into contact with moisture from the hair of mules, donkeys, and other animals. Thus, to hold their hair impure

original_text:
وَالْحَالُ هَذِهِ مِنْ الْحَرَجِ الْمَرْفُوعِ عَنْ الْأُمَّةِ. وَأَيْضًا فَإِنَّ لُعَابَ الْكَلْبِ إذَا أَصَابَ الصَّيْدَ لَمْ يَجِبْ غَسْلُهُ فِي أَظْهَرِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَهُوَ إحْدَى الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَد؛ لِأَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمْ يَأْمُرْ أَحَدًا بِغَسْلِ ذَلِكَ فَقَدْ عفى عَنْ لُعَابِ الْكَلْبِ فِي مَوْضِعِ الْحَاجَةِ وَأَمَرَ بِغَسْلِهِ فِي غَيْرِ مَوْضِعِ الْحَاجَةِ فَدَلَّ عَلَى أَنَّ الشَّارِعَ رَاعَى مَصْلَحَةَ الْخَلْقِ وَحَاجَتَهُمْ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ كَلْبٍ طَلَعَ مِنْ مَاءٍ فَانْتَفَضَ عَلَى شَيْءٍ فَهَلْ يَجِبُ تَسْبِيعُهُ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
مَذْهَبُ الشَّافِعِيِّ وَأَحْمَد رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا يَجِبُ تَسْبِيعُهُ. وَمَذْهَبُ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَمَالِكٍ رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُمَا لَا يَجِبُ تَسْبِيعُهُ وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ سُؤْرِ الْبَغْلِ وَالْحِمَارِ:
 هَلْ هُوَ طَاهِرٌ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
وَأَمَّا سُؤْرُ الْبَغْلِ وَالْحِمَارِ فَأَكْثَرُ الْعُلَمَاءِ يُجَوِّزُونَ التَّوَضُّؤَ بِهِ. كَمَالِكِ وَالشَّافِعِيِّ وَأَحْمَد فِي إحْدَى الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْهُ.
translated_text:
in these circumstances imposes a hardship from which the Muslim community has been relieved. Furthermore, if a dog’s saliva comes into contact with game, it need not be washed off according to the stronger of the two scholarly views, which is also one of the two positions reported from Ahmad. This is because the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, never instructed anyone to wash it off. Thus, he excused a dog’s saliva where there was a need, but commanded that it be washed off where there was no such need. This shows that the Lawgiver took people’s welfare and needs into account. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

If a dog comes out of water and shakes itself over something, must that thing be washed seven times?

He replied:

According to the schools of al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad, may Allah be pleased with them both, it must be washed seven times. According to the schools of Abū Hanīfah and Mālik, may Allah be pleased with them both, washing it seven times is not required. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Is the water left over after a mule or donkey has drunk from it pure?

He replied:

As for the water left over after a mule or donkey has drunk from it, most scholars permit using it for ablution, including Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī, and Ahmad according to one of the two positions reported from him.

original_text:
وَالرِّوَايَةُ الْأُخْرَى عَنْهُ مَشْكُوكٌ فِيهِ. كَقَوْلِ أَبِي حَنِيفَةَ فَيَتَوَضَّأُ بِهِ وَيَتَيَمَّمُ.
 وَالثَّالِثَةُ أَنَّهُ نَجِسٌ لِأَنَّهُ مُتَوَلِّدٌ مِنْ بَاطِنِ حَيَوَانٍ نَجِسٍ فَيَكُونُ نَجِسًا كَلُعَابِ الْكَلْبِ:
 لَكِنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ قَالَ فِي الْهِرَّةِ: 
{إنَّهَا مِنْ الطَّوَّافِينَ عَلَيْكُمْ وَالطَّوَّافَاتِ}
 فَعَلَّلَ طَهَارَةَ سُؤْرِهَا لِكَوْنِهَا مِنْ الطَّوَّافِينَ عَلَيْنَا وَالطَّوَّافَاتِ وَهَذَا يَقْتَضِي أَنَّ الْحَاجَةَ مُقْتَضِيَةٌ لِلطَّهَارَةِ وَهَذَا مِنْ حُجَّةِ مَنْ يُبِيحُ سُؤْرَ الْبَغْلِ وَالْحِمَارِ. فَإِنَّ الْحَاجَةَ دَاعِيَةٌ إلَى ذَلِكَ وَالْمَانِعُ يَقُولُ ذَلِكَ مِثْلُ سُؤْرِ الْكَلْبِ فَإِنَّهُ مَعَ إبَاحَةِ قِنْيَتِهِ لِمَا يُحْتَاجُ فِيهِ إلَيْهِ نُهِيَ عَنْ سُؤْرِهِ.
 وَالْمُرَخِّصُ يَقُولُ:
 إنَّ الْكَلْبَ أَبَاحَهُ لِلْحَاجَةِ وَلِهَذَا حَرَّمَ ثَمَنَهُ؛ بِخِلَافِ الْبَغْلِ وَالْحِمَارِ فَإِنَّ بَيْعَهُمَا جَائِزٌ بِاتِّفَاقِ الْمُسْلِمِينَ. وَالْمَسْأَلَةُ مَبْنِيَّةٌ عَلَى أَسْآرِ السِّبَاعِ وَمَا لَا يُؤْكَلُ لَحْمُهُ.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ طِينِ جَبَلٍ بِزِبْلِ حِمَارٍ وَطُيِّنَ بِهِ سَطْحٌ فَوَقَعَ عَلَيْهِ قَطْرٌ فَتَعَلَّقَ بِهِ مَا حُكْمُهُ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، إنْ كَانَ يَسِيرًا عُفِيَ عَنْهُ. فِي أَحَدِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ.
translated_text:
And according to the other report from him, its purity is doubtful, as in Abū Hanīfah’s view: one performs ablution with it and also performs dry ablution.

A third report holds that it is impure because it comes from within an impure animal, and is therefore impure like a dog’s saliva.

However, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said concerning the cat:

“It is one of those—male and female—who move about among you.”

He thus explained the purity of the water left after a cat drinks by its being among those who move about among us. This indicates that need warrants a ruling of purity. This is part of the argument advanced by those who permit using water left after a mule or donkey has drunk from it, since there is a need for this. Those who prohibit it argue that it is like water left after a dog has drunk: although keeping a dog is permitted for purposes for which it is needed, using the water left after it drinks is prohibited.

Those who allow it respond:

The Prophet permitted keeping a dog because of need, and for this reason forbade taking a price for it. Mules and donkeys are different: selling them is permissible by the agreement of the Muslims. This question rests on the ruling concerning water left after predatory beasts and animals whose meat may not be eaten have drunk from it.

He was asked:

What is the ruling when clay mixed with donkey dung is used to plaster a roof, then rain falls on it and carries some of that mixture with it?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. If the amount is small, it is excused according to one of the two scholarly views.

وَسُئِلَ:
عَمَّا إذَا بَالَ الْفَأْرُ فِي الْفِرَاشِ هَلْ يُصَلَّى فِيهِ؟ .
فَأَجَابَ:
غَسْلُهُ أَحْوَطُ وَيُعْفَى عَنْ يَسِيرِهِ فِي أَحَدِ قَوْلَيْ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَهُوَ إحْدَى الرِّوَايَتَيْنِ عَنْ أَحْمَد.
وَسُئِلَ:
عَنْ رِيشِ الْقُنْفُذِ هَلْ هُوَ نَجِسٌ؟
فَأَجَابَ:
الْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، هُوَ طَاهِرٌ وَإِنْ وُجِدَ بَعْدَ مَوْتِهِ عِنْدَ جُمْهُورِ الْعُلَمَاءِ وَهُوَ مَذْهَبُ مَالِكٍ وَأَبِي حَنِيفَةَ وَأَحْمَد فِي ظَاهِرِ مَذْهَبِهِ.
translated_text:
and this is one of the reports from Ahmad, especially if the dung was mixed with the clay used to plaster the roof, since it may have undergone a transformation. Even if it has not, the amount carried by the raindrops is small.

He was asked:

If a mouse urinates on bedding, may one pray on it?

He replied:

Washing it is more cautious. A small amount is excused according to one of the two scholarly views, which is also one of the two reports from Ahmad.

He was asked:

Are hedgehog quills impure?

He replied:

Praise be to Allah. They are pure according to the majority of scholars, even if found after the hedgehog’s death. This is the view of Mālik and Abū Hanīfah, and the apparent position of Ahmad’s school.

original_text:
بَابٌ الْحَيْضُ:

عَمَّا يُرْوَى عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{الْحَيْضُ لِلْجَارِيَةِ: الْبِكْرِ ثَلَاثَةُ أَيَّامٍ وَلَيَالِيهِنَّ وَأَكْثَرُهُ خَمْسَةَ عَشَرَ}
 هَلْ هُوَ صَحِيحٌ؟ وَمَا تَأْوِيلُهُ عَلَى مَذْهَبِ الشَّافِعِيِّ وَأَحْمَد؟ .

translated_text:
Chapter: Menstruation

Shaykh al-Islām was asked:

Is the following report attributed to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) authentic, and how is it interpreted according to the schools of al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad?

“Menstruation for a virgin girl lasts three days and their nights, and its maximum duration is fifteen days.”

He replied:

Attributing this report to the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) is false. Indeed, it is a fabricated lie, by agreement of the hadith scholars. It is, however, well known as a report transmitted by Abū al-Khuld from Anas, and Abū al-Khuld’s reliability has been questioned.

As for those who hold that the maximum duration of menstruation is fifteen days, as al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad hold, and that its minimum is one day, as al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad hold, or that it has no minimum limit, as Mālik holds, they say:

Nothing concerning this has been established from the Prophet (peace and blessings be upon him) or his Companions. Rather, the matter is determined by usual menstrual patterns, as we have stated.

And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Is intercourse with a menstruating woman permissible or not?

He replied:

Intercourse with a menstruating woman is forbidden by agreement of the imams, as Allah and His Messenger (peace and blessings be upon him) have prohibited it. If a man has intercourse with her while she is menstruating, there is a well-known disagreement over whether he must offer expiation. Scholars also disagree over her performing a ritual bath for the impurity resulting from intercourse separately from the bath for menstruation. Intercourse with a woman experiencing postnatal bleeding is likewise forbidden by agreement of the imams.

He may, however, take sexual pleasure with a menstruating woman or one experiencing postnatal bleeding in the area above the waist-wrapper, whether using his mouth, hand, or foot. Thus, if he rubs himself against her abdomen and ejaculates, that is permissible. Scholars disagree, however, over whether taking sexual pleasure between her thighs is permissible. And Allah knows best.

He was asked:

If a woman’s menstruation ends and she cannot find water with which to bathe, may her husband have intercourse with her before she bathes, without any condition?

He replied:

This is also the meaning of the reports transmitted from the Companions. More than ten Companions—including the caliphs—are reported to have said concerning a woman observing her waiting period: “Her husband has the greater right to take her back so long as she has not bathed following her third menstrual period.”

The Quran supports this. Allah Most High says:

“Do not approach them until they become pure. Then, when they have purified themselves, approach them as Allah has commanded you.”

Mujāhid said that “until they become pure” means until the bleeding ceases, while “when they have purified themselves” means when they have bathed with water. It is exactly as Mujāhid explained.

Allah mentions two endpoints according to the majority reading because His words, “until they become pure,” mark the end of the prohibition arising from menstruation—a prohibition that cannot be lifted by bathing or by any other means. This prohibition ends when the bleeding ceases. Thereafter, intercourse is permissible on condition that she bathes; it does not remain unconditionally forbidden. Hence His words:

“Then, when they have purified themselves, approach them as Allah has commanded you.”

This is comparable to His words:

“If he divorces her, she is not lawful to him thereafter until she marries another husband.”

Marriage to the second husband marks the end of the prohibition arising from the three divorces. Once she marries the second husband, that prohibition ends. However, she is now married to the second husband and is therefore forbidden to the first because of the second husband’s marital right, not because of the three divorces. If the second husband divorces her, the first may marry her.

Allah Most High has said:

“He has not placed upon you any hardship in religion.”

Is there any disagreement among the imams on this matter?

He replied:

Neither hadith abrogates the other, nor is there any contradiction between them.

The first hadith concerns a woman who has an established menstrual pattern and knows its duration. If she then experiences non-menstrual bleeding, she refrains from prayer for the duration of her usual period. Hence he said:

“Refrain from prayer for as many days as you used to menstruate.”

He also said:

“When your period begins, refrain from prayer; then, when its usual duration has passed, wash the blood off yourself and pray.”

The majority of scholars have adopted this hadith as the basis for ruling that a woman with an established menstrual pattern who experiences non-menstrual bleeding should follow her usual pattern. This is the position of Abū Hanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī and Imam Ahmad.

They disagree, however, about a woman who can distinguish black blood from red blood: should she give precedence to distinguishing between the types of blood over her usual menstrual pattern, or to her usual pattern over that distinction? Some give precedence to distinguishing between the types of blood. This is the position of al-Shāfiʿī and of Ahmad according to one of the two reports from him.

Indeed, Abū Hanīfah did not take the distinction between types of blood into account, just as Mālik did not take the usual menstrual pattern into account. Al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad, however, consider both; the disagreement concerns which takes precedence.

As for the second hadith, it does not state that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed her to bathe for every prayer. Rather, he instructed her to bathe without specifying this, and she herself would bathe for every prayer. Bathing for every prayer is recommended, not obligatory, according to the four imams and others, provided that she refrains from prayer for the known days of her menstrual period, then bathes as a woman whose menstruation has ended would bathe, and thereafter prays and fasts despite this non-menstrual bleeding. What is obligatory, according to the majority—including Abū Hanīfah, al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad—is that she perform ablution for each of the five prayers.

Mālik, however, holds that neither ablution nor a full ritual bath is required of her on account of this bleeding, since, in his view, non-menstrual bleeding does not invalidate ablution, nor do other unusual discharges. The majority cite as evidence the report in al-Tirmidhī and elsewhere:

“The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, instructed the woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding to perform ablution for every prayer.”

The woman in the second hadith was not experiencing menstruation for the first time, although some people have supposed this, for she was an elderly woman. Rather, they understood her case as that of a woman who had forgotten her usual menstrual pattern. The Sunan collections state:

“She was instructed to treat six or seven days as her menstrual period.”

Ahmad and others relied in arguing that a woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding who can distinguish between the types of blood should refrain from prayer for six or seven days, the usual duration of menstruation.

Three teachings have been transmitted from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, concerning women experiencing non-menstrual bleeding: one concerns the usual menstrual pattern, as discussed above; another concerns a woman who can distinguish between the types of blood, namely his statement:

“Menstrual blood is black and recognizable.”

The third concerns the usual duration of menstruation, namely his statement:

“Treat six or seven days as your menstrual period, then bathe and pray for twenty-three or twenty-four days, just as women menstruate and become pure according to their regular times of menstruation and purity.”

Scholars disagree concerning non-menstrual bleeding, for it is a difficult matter: menstrual blood can be confused with non-menstrual blood, so there must be a criterion distinguishing the two.

Six indicators have been proposed:

One is the usual menstrual pattern, which is the strongest indicator, because the presumption is that menstruation, rather than other bleeding, persists during that period. Another is distinguishing between the types of blood, since black, thick, foul-smelling blood is more likely to be menstrual than red blood. Another is considering the usual menstrual pattern of most women, for the basic principle is to treat an individual case according to what is most general

and prevalent. These three indicators are supported by the Sunnah and sound reasoning. Some jurists have her refrain from prayer for one night, the minimum duration of menstruation. Others have her refrain for its maximum duration, because the presumption is that the bleeding is normal, healthy bleeding. Still others have her follow the menstrual pattern of the women in her family. There is disagreement over whether this ruling applies only to a woman who has forgotten her menstrual pattern, or both to her and to a woman menstruating for the first time.

The soundest view is to consider the indicators established by the Sunnah and disregard all others. As for a woman who can distinguish between the types of blood, she should refrain from prayer for the usual duration of menstruation, as established by the Sunnah. Anyone who declines to classify any of her bleeding as menstruation, instead requiring her to take precautionary measures in every circumstance, has imposed an enormous burden upon her, the like of which the Sharia does not prescribe. This makes worshipping Allah hateful to those who follow His religion, whereas Allah has removed hardship from the Muslims. This is among the very weakest opinions.

The underlying principle is that blood, in terms of its legal ruling, falls into no more than five categories:

Blood that is certainly menstrual, such as regular menstrual blood unaccompanied by non-menstrual bleeding.

Blood that is certainly non-menstrual, such as the blood of a young girl.

Blood that could be either, but is more likely to be menstrual. This is the blood of a woman with an established menstrual pattern

{وَمَا كَانَ اللَّهُ لِيُضِلَّ قَوْمًا بَعْدَ إذْ هَدَاهُمْ حَتَّى يُبَيِّنَ لَهُمْ مَا يَتَّقُونَ}
 فَاَللَّهُ تَعَالَى قَدْ بَيَّنَ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ فِي الْمُسْتَحَاضَةِ وَغَيْرِهَا مَا تَتَّقِيهِ مِنْ الصَّلَاةِ وَالصِّيَامِ فِي زَمَنِ الْحَيْضِ فَكَيْفَ يُقَالُ: إنَّ الشَّرِيعَةَ فِيهَا شَكٌّ مُسْتَمِرٌّ يَحْكُمُ بِهِ الرَّسُولُ وَأُمَّتُهُ نَعَمْ: قَدْ يَكُونُ شَكٌّ خَاصٌّ بِبَعْضِ النَّاسِ. كَاَلَّذِي يَشُكُّ هَلْ أَحْدَثَ أَمْ لَا؟ كَالشُّبُهَاتِ الَّتِي لَا يَعْلَمُهَا كَثِيرٌ مِنْ النَّاسِ فَأَمَّا شَكٌّ وَشُبْهَةٌ تَكُونُ فِي نَفْسِ الشَّرِيعَةِ فَهَذَا بَاطِلٌ وَاَلَّذِينَ يَجْعَلُونَ هَذَا دَم شَكٍّ يَجْعَلُونَ ذَلِكَ حُكْمَ الشَّرْعِ؛
 لَا يَقُولُونَ:
 نَحْنُ شَكَكْنَا؛ فَإِنَّ الشَّاكَّ لَا عِلْمَ عِنْدِهِ فَلَا يَجْزِمُ وَهَؤُلَاءِ يَجْزِمُونَ بِوُجُوبِ الصِّيَامِ وَإِعَادَتِهِ لِشَكِّهِمْ.
 الْوَجْهُ الثَّانِي:
 أَنَّ الشَّرِيعَةَ لَيْسَ فِيهَا إيجَابُ الصَّلَاةِ مَرَّتَيْنِ وَلَا
translated_text:
and of a woman who can distinguish between the types of blood, and similar women experiencing non-menstrual bleeding—blood that is ruled to be menstrual.

Blood that could be either, but is more likely to be abnormal bleeding. This is the blood of these women that is ruled to be non-menstrual.

Blood whose status is uncertain, with neither possibility outweighing the other. A group of scholars among the followers of al-Shāfiʿī, Ahmad and others recognizes this category. They require a woman affected by it to fast and pray, and then make up the fasts. The correct view is that this opinion is invalid for several reasons:

First: Allah Most High says:

“Allah would never let a people go astray after He has guided them until He makes clear to them what they must avoid.”

Allah Most High has explained to the Muslims what a woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding, or any other woman, must refrain from during menstruation: prayer and fasting. How, then, can it be said that the Sharia contains a state of perpetual uncertainty upon which the Messenger and his community base their rulings? Certainly, particular individuals may experience uncertainty, as when someone doubts whether he has invalidated his state of ritual purity, or concerning doubtful matters of which many people have no knowledge. But uncertainty and ambiguity inherent in the Sharia itself—this is untenable. Those who classify this blood as uncertain make that classification a ruling of the Sharia. They do not say, “We are uncertain.” Someone who is uncertain has no knowledge and therefore cannot make a categorical assertion. Yet these scholars categorically assert that fasting and repeating it are obligatory because of their uncertainty.

Second: The Sharia does not require prayer to be performed twice, nor

fasting twice, except when the worshipper has been negligent. Where there has been no negligence, Allah has not required two months of fasting in a year or two noon prayers in a day. This demonstrates the weakness of the view that requires someone both to perform a prayer and to repeat it. This is a weak principle, as has been discussed at length elsewhere. It includes requiring someone to pray behind an openly sinful imam and then repeat the prayer; to pray despite rare impediments that do not persist and then repeat the prayer; or requiring a woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding to fast twice. Such rulings are found in the schools of al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad, according to one of the two views.

The correct position, held by the majority of Muslims, is that whoever performs an act of worship as commanded, to the best of their ability, need not repeat it. As Allah Most High says:

“So fear Allah as much as you are able.”

It has never been known that the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, commanded anyone to perform the same prayer twice. Rather, he would command someone to repeat it if they had failed to do what they were commanded despite being able to do so. Thus, he said to the man who prayed incorrectly:

“Go back and pray, for you have not prayed.”

Likewise, he commanded the man who prayed alone behind the row to repeat his prayer.

As for those with a valid excuse—such as someone who performs dry ablution because water is unavailable, or because using it could cause harm due to illness or cold; a woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding; and others like them—the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, is that they do whatever they can, according to their ability, while whatever lies beyond their ability is waived. Indeed, his Sunnah regarding someone who was unaware of an obligation is that there is no requirement to make it up

{صَلِّ قَائِمًا فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَقَاعِدًا فَإِنْ لَمْ تَسْتَطِعْ فَعَلَى جَنْبٍ}
 وَهَذِهِ قَاعِدَةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ تَحْتَاجُ إلَى بَسْطٍ لَيْسَ هَذَا مَوْضِعَهُ.
translated_text:
on their part, because religious obligation is conditional upon the ability to acquire knowledge and to perform the act. This is why he did not command ʿUmar and ʿAmmār to repeat their prayers when they were in a state of major ritual impurity. ʿUmar did not pray, while ʿAmmār rolled in the dust as an animal does, thinking that the dust should reach wherever water would reach. Likewise, he did not command those Companions who continued eating until they could distinguish black cords from white ones to make up their fasts.

Similarly, he did not command those who prayed in a direction other than the Kaaba before news of the change in ruling reached them to repeat their prayers. Some were in Abyssinia, some in Mecca, and others elsewhere. Indeed, even some of those in Medina performed part of their prayer facing the Kaaba and part facing the Rock, yet he did not command them to repeat it. There are numerous similar examples.

Anyone who thoroughly examines what the Quran and Sunnah have brought will see that religious obligation is conditional upon the ability to know and to act. Whoever is incapable of either is relieved of whatever lies beyond their ability:

“Allah does not burden any soul beyond its capacity.”

This is why someone who errs in exercising independent judgment is excused: they were unable to ascertain the truth in that particular matter. This is unlike someone who is negligent despite being able to do what they were commanded; that is the person who deserves punishment.

This is why the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said to ʿImrān ibn Husayn:

“Pray standing; if you cannot, then sitting; and if you cannot, then lying on your side.”

This is a major principle that requires an extensive discussion, for which this is not the place.

{وَإِنْ كُنْتُمْ جُنُبًا فَاطَّهَّرُوا}
 وَقَدْ رُوِيَ مَا يَدُلُّ عَلَى ذَلِكَ عَنْ أَكَابِرِ الصَّحَابَةِ: كَعُمَرِ وَعُثْمَانَ وَعَلِيٍّ وَابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَأَبِي مُوسَى وَغَيْرِهِمْ حَيْثُ جَعَلُوا الزَّوْجَ أَحَقَّ بِهَا مَا لَمْ تَغْتَسِلْ مِنْ الْحَيْضَةِ الثَّالِثَةِ. وَأَمَّا أَبُو حَنِيفَةَ فَمَذْهَبُهُ إنْ انْقَطَعَ الدَّمُ لِعَشَرَةِ أَيَّامٍ أَوْ أَكْثَرَ وَمَرَّ عَلَيْهَا وَقْتُ صَلَاةٍ أَوْ اغْتَسَلَتْ وَطِئَهَا وَإِلَّا فَلَا. وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
The questioner’s concern is with a woman experiencing non-menstrual bleeding. We have explained that the correct view is that under no circumstances is she required both to fast and to make up that fast, as some followers of al-Shāfiʿī, Ahmad and others require in certain cases. Nor is she required to perform the ritual bath for every prayer, by agreement of the four imams and others. Allah knows best.

He was asked:

Regarding a woman with postnatal bleeding who has not performed the ritual bath: is intercourse with her permissible before she bathes?

He answered:

Intercourse with a menstruating woman or a woman with postnatal bleeding is not permissible until she has performed the ritual bath. If she cannot find water, or fears harm from using it because of illness or severe cold, she should perform dry ablution, after which intercourse with her is permissible. This is the position of the great majority of the imams, including Mālik, al-Shāfiʿī and Ahmad.

The Quran indicates this in the words of the Most High:

“Do not approach them until they are pure,”

meaning until the bleeding stops;

“Then, when they have purified themselves,”

meaning when they have bathed with water. Likewise, He says:

“If you are in a state of major ritual impurity, purify yourselves.”

Reports supporting this have been transmitted from leading Companions, including ʿUmar, ʿUthmān, ʿAlī, Ibn Masʿūd, Abū Mūsā and others. They held that the husband had the greater claim to her so long as she had not bathed after her third menstrual period.

As for Abū Hanīfah, his position is that if the bleeding stops after ten days or more, and a prayer time has elapsed for her or she has performed the ritual bath, he may have intercourse with her; otherwise, he may not. Allah knows best.

translated_text:
He—may Allah have mercy on him—was asked:

Regarding a woman experiencing postnatal bleeding: may she recite the Quran during this bleeding? Is intercourse with her permissible before forty days have elapsed? If forty days have elapsed but she has not performed the ritual bath, is intercourse with her permissible without her bathing?

He answered:

Praise be to Allah. Intercourse with her before the bleeding stops is forbidden by agreement of the imams. If the bleeding stops before forty days have elapsed, she must perform the ritual bath and pray. Her husband, however, should refrain from intercourse with her until the forty days are complete.

As for reciting the Quran, if she does not fear forgetting it, she should not recite it. If she fears forgetting it, she may recite it according to one of the two scholarly views. Once the bleeding has stopped and she has performed the ritual bath, she may recite the Quran and pray, by scholarly agreement. If she is unable to bathe because water is unavailable, or because she fears harm due to illness or the like, she should perform dry ablution. She may then do whatever the ritual bath would permit her to do. Allah knows best.
